1	// Package natslog picks the severity a NATS pull-consumer failure warrants.
     2	//
     3	// The premise: a dropped link, a drained connection, a consumer that moved —
     4	// the consume loops absorb all of these by retrying with backoff, and none of
     5	// them is something an operator can act on. Left at error level they are not
     6	// merely untidy, they are load-bearing in the wrong direction: one
     7	// mirror-pipeline pod emitted 57 ErrNoResponders inside 83 milliseconds as its
     8	// in-flight fetches failed together during a deploy, and two services between
     9	// them tripped a cluster's error-log alert three times in forty minutes. Every
    10	// one of those alerts was accurate about the count and wrong about the
    11	// meaning, which is how a signal stops being read (COR-1228). The same
    12	// reasoning previously lived as hand-rolled ErrStreamNotFound warn-branches in
    13	// each subscribe loop; those now route here too.
    14	//
    15	// The demotion is not unconditional, because "recoverable" is a claim about
    16	// what happens next, not a property of the error value: the same
    17	// ErrNoResponders means deploy churn when the next fetch succeeds and a down
    18	// JetStream when nothing has succeeded for ten minutes. Each consumer loop
    19	// holds a [Health] that its success path resets ([Health.Recovered]); a loop
    20	// whose failures keep arriving with no recovery in between returns to error
    21	// level after [escalateAfter], so a sustained outage still pages while
    22	// absorbed churn — however long it goes on — stays quiet.
    23	//
    24	// Escalation state is per-process, so a fleet whose pods restart faster than
    25	// escalateAfter would never escalate from logs alone. Every recoverable
    26	// failure therefore also increments the nats.consumer.recoverable_failures
    27	// counter, which survives restarts by construction; rate-alert on that for
    28	// the restart-storm case.
    29	package natslog
    30	
    31	import (
    32		"context"
    33		"errors"
    34		"log/slog"
    35		"runtime"
    36		"sync"
    37		"time"
    38	
    39		nuts "github.com/entireio/go-nuts"
    40		"github.com/nats-io/nats.go"
    41		"github.com/nats-io/nats.go/jetstream"
    42		"go.opentelemetry.io/otel"
    43		"go.opentelemetry.io/otel/attribute"
    44		"go.opentelemetry.io/otel/metric"
    45	)
    46	
    47	// escalateAfter is how long a loop may keep failing with no recovery in
    48	// between before its failures stop being "transient" and return to error
    49	// level. Deploy and NATS-upgrade interruptions resolve in seconds; nothing
    50	// routine keeps a single consumer loop failing continuously for this long.
    51	const escalateAfter = 5 * time.Minute
    52	
    53	// msgStreamNotYetPresent is the canonical rollout-ordering line. It predates
    54	// this package (the subscribe loops each carried a hand-rolled warn branch
    55	// emitting it), and external tooling keys on the literal text, so it is
    56	// preserved verbatim here rather than folded into the caller's message.
    57	const msgStreamNotYetPresent = "Stream not yet present, retrying"
    58	
    59	// now is swapped by tests to drive the escalation clock.
    60	var now = time.Now
    61	
    62	// Health tracks one consumer loop's failure run: how long failures have been
    63	// arriving since the loop last made progress. One Health per loop — the
    64	// question it answers is "has THIS loop stopped recovering", and pooling
    65	// loops would let one loop's health mask another's outage.
    66	//
    67	// The zero value is healthy and ready to use.
    68	type Health struct {
    69		mu        sync.Mutex
    70		firstFail time.Time
    71	}
    72	
    73	// Recovered marks the loop healthy, ending any failure run. Call it where the
    74	// loop demonstrably makes progress — a fetch that returned messages or timed
    75	// out idle (an idle poll proves the consumer is connected and the stream is
    76	// merely quiet), or a backstop subscription that established.
    77	func (h *Health) Recovered() {
    78		h.mu.Lock()
    79		h.firstFail = time.Time{}
    80		h.mu.Unlock()
    81	}
    82	
    83	// failingFor records a recoverable failure and reports how long the loop has
    84	// been failing without recovery.
    85	func (h *Health) failingFor(t time.Time) time.Duration {
    86		h.mu.Lock()
    87		defer h.mu.Unlock()
    88		if h.firstFail.IsZero() {
    89			h.firstFail = t
    90		}
    91		return t.Sub(h.firstFail)
    92	}
    93	
    94	// Err logs a fetch failure at the severity its recoverability warrants: warn
    95	// while the retry loop absorbs it, error for faults — or for a recoverable
    96	// failure once the loop has gone [escalateAfter] without [Health.Recovered].
    97	//
    98	// It deliberately does not decide control flow. Callers keep their existing
    99	// return-and-resubscribe or continue-with-backoff behaviour; only the
   100	// severity changes, so this cannot alter how the consumers recover. The error
   101	// attribute is always emitted first, before attrs.
   102	func (h *Health) Err(ctx context.Context, msg string, err error, attrs ...slog.Attr) {
   103		h.classify(ctx, msg, err, attrs, nuts.IsTransientFetchErr(err), "fetch", callerPC())
   104	}
   105	
   106	// SubscribeErr is [Health.Err] for subscribe/create retry paths, which absorb
   107	// two failures a fetch path must not: a JetStream API slow to answer the
   108	// consumer-info/create request (deploy churn), and the stream not existing
   109	// yet. The latter is rollout ordering — the consumer up before the service
   110	// that ensures the stream — and is an expected state, not a failure run: it
   111	// keeps the canonical "Stream not yet present, retrying" message, stays at
   112	// warn no matter how long it lasts (a dev cluster may never grow the stream),
   113	// and does not feed escalation.
   114	func (h *Health) SubscribeErr(ctx context.Context, msg string, err error, attrs ...slog.Attr) {
   115		if errors.Is(err, nats.ErrStreamNotFound) || errors.Is(err, jetstream.ErrStreamNotFound) {
   116			emit(ctx, slog.LevelWarn, msgStreamNotYetPresent, err, attrs, 0, callerPC())
   117			return
   118		}
   119		h.classify(ctx, msg, err, attrs, isTransientSubscribeErr(err), "subscribe", callerPC())
   120	}
   121	
   122	// isTransientSubscribeErr extends [nuts.IsTransientSubscribeErr] with the modern
   123	// jetstream client's equivalents.
   124	//
   125	// The go-nuts predicate keys on the LEGACY nats.* error values, and the
   126	// jetstream package defines its own distinct ones — jetstream.ErrStreamNotFound
   127	// is a *jsError carrying an APIError, not nats.ErrStreamNotFound — so
   128	// errors.Is finds neither across the two. A consumer migrated to the modern
   129	// client (COR-1254) would therefore have every rollout-ordering failure
   130	// classified as a FAULT and logged at error, which is precisely the alert-eroding
   131	// noise this package exists to prevent (COR-1228).
   132	//
   133	// ErrJetStreamNotEnabled is a 503 from a server that has not finished bringing
   134	// JetStream up — a restart, not a misconfiguration, and the escalation clock
   135	// catches it if it never resolves.
   136	//
   137	// A MISSING CONSUMER is deliberately NOT here, and that asymmetry is the point.
   138	// This package already keeps nats.ErrConsumerDeleted at error level because a
   139	// durable that disappears is recreated by its supervisor from the stream's
   140	// DeliverPolicy, losing the cursor and replaying whatever the stream still
   141	// retains — the loudest thing a consumer loop can do quietly. The modern
   142	// spellings (ErrConsumerNotFound, ErrConsumerDoesNotExist) mean exactly that
   143	// once a consumer has bound, so demoting them here would silence it.
   144	//
   145	// They ARE expected before the first successful bind, while the supervisor is
   146	// still creating the durable — but only the caller knows which side of that line
   147	// it is on, so the caller makes the distinction (see the lifecycle fan's
   148	// readiness probe) rather than this predicate guessing from the error value. That
   149	// is the same reasoning as the package doc's: recoverable is a claim about what
   150	// happens next, not a property of the error.
   151	//
   152	// This belongs in go-nuts beside the predicate it extends; kept here until the
   153	// modern-client migration has more than one adopter to generalise from.
   154	func isTransientSubscribeErr(err error) bool {
   155		return nuts.IsTransientSubscribeErr(err) ||
   156			errors.Is(err, jetstream.ErrJetStreamNotEnabled)
   157	}
   158	
   159	func (h *Health) classify(ctx context.Context, msg string, err error, attrs []slog.Attr, recoverable bool, path string, pc uintptr) {
   160		level := slog.LevelError
   161		var failingFor time.Duration
   162		if recoverable {
   163			level = slog.LevelWarn
   164			if failingFor = h.failingFor(now()); failingFor >= escalateAfter {
   165				level = slog.LevelError
   166			}
   167			recoverableFailures().Add(ctx, 1, metric.WithAttributes(attribute.String("path", path)))
   168		}
   169		emit(ctx, level, msg, err, attrs, failingFor, pc)
   170	}
   171	
   172	func emit(ctx context.Context, level slog.Level, msg string, err error, attrs []slog.Attr, failingFor time.Duration, pc uintptr) {
   173		logger := slog.Default()
   174		if !logger.Enabled(ctx, level) {
   175			return
   176		}
   177		r := slog.NewRecord(now(), level, msg, pc)
   178		r.AddAttrs(slog.Any("error", err))
   179		if failingFor >= escalateAfter {
   180			r.AddAttrs(slog.Duration("failing_for", failingFor))
   181		}
   182		r.AddAttrs(attrs...)
   183		_ = logger.Handler().Handle(ctx, r)
   184	}
   185	
   186	// callerPC captures the PC of the exported method's caller, so the record's
   187	// source location is the consumer loop that failed rather than this file —
   188	// several loops share the literal message "Fetch error", and under AddSource
   189	// the PC is what tells them apart. Skip runtime.Callers, callerPC, and the
   190	// exported method.
   191	func callerPC() uintptr {
   192		var pcs [1]uintptr
   193		runtime.Callers(3, pcs[:])
   194		return pcs[0]
   195	}
   196	
   197	// recoverableFailures counts every failure this package demotes below error
   198	// level. Log-side escalation lives in process memory and dies with the pod,
   199	// so a sustained outage under a restart storm (crashloops, rollout-restart
   200	// attempts — incident conditions) would otherwise never produce an
   201	// error-level signal; a rate alert on this counter is the restart-proof
   202	// complement. by path=fetch|subscribe.
   203	var recoverableFailures = sync.OnceValue(func() metric.Int64Counter {
   204		c, _ := otel.Meter("github.com/entirehq/mirror-pipeline/internal/natslog").Int64Counter(
   205			"nats.consumer.recoverable_failures",
   206			metric.WithDescription("Recoverable NATS consumer interruptions demoted below error level, "+
   207				"by path=fetch|subscribe. Sustained rate = a consumer failing to recover; "+
   208				"alert on this for outages whose pod restarts outpace log-side escalation."),
   209		)
   210		return c
   211	})

   328		// echo that recirculated at ~16.5/s across all cells. Ack and stop here. This

   368	// source stream + sequence (also stable for a given stored message) so a

   374				return id
   375			}
   376		}

   381	}

   388			out[k] = append([]string(nil), v...)
   389		}
   390		return out
   391	}

   272	func (c *lifecycleConsumer) handleMessage(ctx context.Context, msg *nats.Msg) {
   273		ctx = natsmsg.Extract(ctx, msg)
   274		ctx, span := otel.Tracer(tracerName).Start(ctx, "meta_fanout.lifecycle_fan",
   275			trace.WithSpanKind(trace.SpanKindConsumer),
   276			trace.WithAttributes(
   277				attribute.String("messaging.system", "nats"),
   278				attribute.String("messaging.operation.type", "receive"),
   279				attribute.String("messaging.destination.name", msg.Subject),
   280			),
   281		)
   282		defer span.End()
   283	
   284		if meta, err := msg.Metadata(); err == nil {
   285			span.SetAttributes(
   286				attribute.Int64("messaging.nats.sequence", int64(meta.Sequence.Stream)),
   287				attribute.Int64("messaging.nats.delivery_count", int64(meta.NumDelivered)),

   298		// crashes the process, and because the message was never acked JetStream
   299		// redelivers it — so every replica that picks it up crashes in turn, turning
   300		// one poison-pill delivery into a cluster-wide crash-loop. Recover and Nak
   301		// (bounded by MaxDeliver) instead.
   302		defer func() {
   303			if r := recover(); r != nil {
   304				err := fmt.Errorf("panic recovered in lifecycle handler: %v", r)
   305				span.RecordError(err)
   306				span.SetStatus(otelcodes.Error, "handler panic")
   307				span.SetAttributes(attribute.Bool("entire.handler.panicked", true))
   308				slog.ErrorContext(ctx, "Recovered panic in lifecycle handler; naking delivery (bounded by MaxDeliver)",

   311				_ = msg.NakWithDelay(consumerFailureDelay)
   312			}
   313		}()
   314	
   315		span.SetAttributes(attribute.String("entire.lifecycle.subject", subject))
   316	
   317		// Additive to the verbatim fan: on a mirror.created, enqueue a github_meta
   318		// backfill so a new mirror gets its display metadata without a webhook or a
   319		// manual run (COR-717). Best-effort by design — it never touches the ack
   320		// disposition below, which stays governed solely by the fan. Run before the
   321		// fan so a delivery the fan will Nak (remote region down) still seeds; the
   322		// backfill dedup id makes the redelivery idempotent.
   323		c.maybeSeedMirrorMeta(ctx, span, subject, data)
   324	
   325		// One-generation fan (COR-902): if this event already carries the fanned-by
   326		// marker it is a cross-region copy some cell exported (possibly ours, hops
   327		// ago), so do NOT re-export it — re-fanning imported copies is exactly the
   328		// echo that recirculated at ~16.5/s across all cells. Ack and stop here. This
   329		// runs AFTER maybeSeedMirrorMeta on purpose: a foreign-origin mirror.created
   330		// reaches US only as a fanned copy and US is where the github_meta seed runs
   331		// (COR-717), so the seed must still fire for marked messages. And it does not
   332		// affect downstream consumers — the event is already in this cell's stream
   333		// where entire-api's repolifecycle / mirror-lifecycle / settings consumers
   334		// read it (COR-901); only the re-EXPORT is suppressed.
   335		if _, marked := header[lifecycleFannedByHeader]; marked {
   336			span.SetAttributes(attribute.Bool("entire.lifecycle.fanned_in", true))
   337			c.metrics.recordLifecycleFan(ctx, dispatchOutcomeSkippedForeign)
   338			_ = msg.Ack()
   339			return
   340		}
   341	
   342		if err := c.fanout.fan(ctx, subject, lifecycleMsgID(header, msg), data, header); err != nil {
   343			// A region was unreachable. NakWithDelay so JetStream redelivers after
   344			// the flat consumerFailureDelay; acking would drop the only durable copy
   345			// of the event before it reached every region. On the final delivery the
   346			// Nak is dropped silently at MaxDeliver (no DLQ — the source stream
   347			// retains the event and replay is a separate path).
   348			span.RecordError(err)
   349			span.SetStatus(otelcodes.Error, "lifecycle fan")
   350			slog.WarnContext(ctx, "Lifecycle fan failed; will redeliver",
   351				slog.String("subject", subject),
   352				slog.Int("delivery", numDelivered(msg)),
   353				slog.Duration("redeliver_in", consumerFailureDelay),
   354				slog.Any("error", err))
   355			c.metrics.recordLifecycleFan(ctx, dispatchOutcomeNak)
   356			_ = msg.NakWithDelay(consumerFailureDelay)
   357			return
   358		}
   359	
   360		c.metrics.recordLifecycleFan(ctx, dispatchOutcomeAck)
   361		_ = msg.Ack()
   362		slog.InfoContext(ctx, "Fanned lifecycle event", slog.String("subject", subject))
   363	}
   364	
   365	// lifecycleMsgID returns the dedup key carried onto the fanned copies. It
   366	// prefers the source event's own Nats-Msg-Id (stable across the source's
   367	// redeliveries and semantically the same logical event), falling back to the
   368	// source stream + sequence (also stable for a given stored message) so a
   369	// republish always collapses on the remote dedup window. Empty only for a
   370	// synthetic message with neither, in which case dedup is simply not applied.
   371	func lifecycleMsgID(srcHeader nats.Header, msg ackableMsg) string {
   372		if srcHeader != nil {
   373			if id := srcHeader.Get(metajobs.NatsMsgIDHeader); id != "" {
   374				return id
   375			}
   376		}
   377		if meta, err := msg.Metadata(); err == nil {
   378			return lifecycleStream + ":" + strconv.FormatUint(meta.Sequence.Stream, 10)
   379		}
   380		return ""
   381	}
   382	
   383	// cloneHeader deep-copies a nats.Header so per-region trace injection does not
   384	// mutate the shared source header. A nil source yields an empty, writable map.
   385	func cloneHeader(h nats.Header) nats.Header {
   386		out := make(nats.Header, len(h))
   387		for k, v := range h {
   388			out[k] = append([]string(nil), v...)
   389		}
   390		return out
   391	}

180	// lifecycleConsumer drains the LOCAL resource_lifecycle_v1 stream and fans each
   181	// event cross-region. Its own durable keeps it isolated from the github_meta
   182	// webhook and backfill consumers on their own streams. The ack discipline
   183	// mirrors the github_meta consumer: explicit ManualAck with a bounded AckWait
   184	// and MaxDeliver, NakWithDelay on a transient fan failure, Ack on success.
   185	// There is no Term path — the event is republished verbatim, so nothing about
   186	// it can be permanently unprocessable.
   187	type lifecycleConsumer struct {
   188		js      nats.JetStreamContext
   189		fanout  *lifecycleFanout
   190		metrics *metaFanoutMetrics
   191		durable string
   192		subject string
   193		// health drives the severity of subscribe/fetch failure logs: recoverable
   194		// interruptions log at warn until the loop goes too long without progress.
   195		health natslog.Health
   196	
   197		// enqueuer + resolver drive the additive mirror.created → github_meta seed
   198		// (COR-717). Both nil leaves the consumer a pure cross-region fan (its
   199		// original behavior), so fan-only tests need not wire them.
   200		enqueuer backfillEnqueuer
   201		resolver mirrorResolver
   202	
   203		// subscribed mirrors the github_meta consumer's /readyz gate: a pod that can
   204		// dial NATS but cannot PullSubscribe (auth/perm/durable-config problem) is
   205		// reported NotReady instead of silently looping on backoff.
   206		subscribed atomic.Bool
   207	}
   208	
   209	// Ready returns true while the consumer holds a live pull subscription.
   210	func (c *lifecycleConsumer) Ready() bool { return c.subscribed.Load() }
   211	
   212	func (c *lifecycleConsumer) run(ctx context.Context) {
   213		backoff := consumerBackoffInit
   214		for {
   215			c.subscribed.Store(false)
   216			sub, err := c.js.PullSubscribe(c.subject, c.durable,
   217				nats.ManualAck(),
   218				nats.AckWait(consumerAckWait),
   219				nats.MaxDeliver(consumerMaxDeliver),
   220			)
   221			if err != nil {
   222				c.health.SubscribeErr(ctx, "Lifecycle subscribe failed", err,
   223					slog.String("subject", c.subject), slog.String("durable", c.durable))
   224				select {
   225				case <-ctx.Done():
   226					return
   227				case <-time.After(backoff):
   228					backoff = min(backoff*2, consumerBackoffMax)
   229					continue
   230				}
   231			}
   232			backoff = consumerBackoffInit
   233			c.subscribed.Store(true)
   234			slog.Info("Lifecycle subscribed", slog.String("subject", c.subject), slog.String("durable", c.durable))
   235	
   236			c.consumeLoop(ctx, sub)
   237			c.subscribed.Store(false)
   238	
   239			if ctx.Err() != nil {
   240				return
   241			}
   242		}
   243	}
   244	
   245	func (c *lifecycleConsumer) consumeLoop(ctx context.Context, sub *nats.Subscription) {
   246		for {
   247			if ctx.Err() != nil {
   248				return
   249			}
   250			msgs, err := sub.Fetch(1, nats.MaxWait(5*time.Second))
   251			if err != nil {
   252				if errors.Is(err, nats.ErrTimeout) {
   253					// An idle poll is progress: connected, stream merely quiet.
   254					c.health.Recovered()
   255					continue
   256				}
   257				// This loop lacked the shutdown guard its siblings carry, so a
   258				// clean teardown surfaced as a fault here.
   259				if nuts.IsShutdownFetchErr(ctx, err) {
   260					return
   261				}
   262				c.health.Err(ctx, "Lifecycle fetch error", err)
   263				return
   264			}
   265			c.health.Recovered()
   266			for _, msg := range msgs {
   267				c.handleMessage(ctx, msg)
   268			}
   269		}
   270	}

70	// Config describes the durable consumer to create and how to trace/log it. The
    71	// filter is given as either FilterSubject (single) or FilterSubjects (multi),
    72	// mirroring jetstream.ConsumerConfig, so a migrated consumer preserves its
    73	// existing on-server filter form exactly.
    74	type Config struct {
    75		Stream         string        // JetStream stream to bind (must already exist)
    76		Durable        string        // durable consumer name, stable across restarts
    77		FilterSubject  string        // set this OR FilterSubjects
    78		FilterSubjects []string      // set this OR FilterSubject
    79		AckWait        time.Duration // 0 → DefaultAckWait (see EffectiveAckWait)
    80		MaxDeliver     int           // 0 → DefaultMaxDeliver (see EffectiveMaxDeliver)
    81		SpanName       string        // per-message consumer span name (e.g. "repolifecycle.consume")
    82		Name           string        // short consumer name, used as the log prefix
    83	
    84		// InactiveThreshold mirrors jetstream.ConsumerConfig.InactiveThreshold:
    85		// how long the durable may go without an active subscription before the
    86		// server deletes it; zero means never (the JetStream default for
    87		// durables) UNLESS the stream sets ConsumerLimits.InactiveThreshold — see
    88		// the note below. Consumers on interest-retention streams set this so a
    89		// decommissioned durable stops pinning every message it would have
    90		// received, instead of holding them until the stream's MaxAge.
    91		InactiveThreshold time.Duration
    92	
    93		// MaxAckPending mirrors jetstream.ConsumerConfig.MaxAckPending: the
    94		// server-side cap on deliveries outstanding un-acked across ALL replicas
    95		// sharing the durable; zero uses the server default (1000), or the stream's
    96		// ConsumerLimits.MaxAckPending when it sets one — see the note below.
    97		// Distinct from MaxMessages below, which caps only this process's
    98		// client-side buffer.
    99		//
   100		// # Stream ConsumerLimits fill in both zeros
   101		//
   102		// A stream may carry ConsumerLimits, and the server applies them to any
   103		// consumer that left the matching field zero. So on such a stream neither
   104		// zero above means what it says: this scaffold's consumers inherit the
   105		// STREAM's MaxAckPending instead of 1000, and — the consequential one — an
   106		// InactiveThreshold instead of never, which gives the durable a deletion
   107		// timer nobody here asked for. A durable deleted that way is recreated from
   108		// the stream's DeliverPolicy (all, by default) and replays the retained
   109		// backlog, so the cost of the surprise is a replay, not just a gap.
   110		//
   111		// Set both explicitly on a stream with ConsumerLimits, and read the
   112		// durable's STORED config rather than assuming either field above is what is
   113		// running. Requests that leave them unset are also what pedantic-mode
   114		// clients reject outright (NACK's controller drives fleet Consumer CRs that
   115		// way), so a config this scaffold applies quietly can fail to reconcile in
   116		// the cluster. Measured in internal/brokersemantics
   117		// (TestStreamConsumerLimitsAreInheritedBySilentConsumers).
   118		MaxAckPending int
   119	
   120		// BackOff mirrors jetstream.ConsumerConfig.BackOff: the redelivery
   121		// ladder, one delay per redelivery, applied in place of AckWait. The
   122		// server owns redelivery — this is the one schedule, and [Retry] defers to
   123		// it by leaving a failed delivery untouched rather than running a
   124		// competing one client-side. JetStream
   125		// repeats the last rung once the array runs out, so a short list under a
   126		// larger MaxDeliver is not a short ladder.
   127		//
   128		// Setting it alongside Retry is the intended combination. Its coherence —
   129		// total time to the dead-letter branch, agreement with AckWait, rung count
   130		// against MaxDeliver — is checked at Start through [Schedule], the same
   131		// function fleet CI runs over a rendered NACK Consumer CR.
   132		//
   133		// Leaving it nil is a choice, not a default: the broker still redelivers,
   134		// on AckWait, so the effective ladder becomes AckWait repeated up to
   135		// MaxDeliver. [Schedule] models it that way and holds it to the same
   136		// bounds, which is usually how an unset BackOff gets caught — an AckWait
   137		// sized for one RPC makes a fast, tight retry loop, and one sized for a
   138		// slow handler makes a very long one.
   139		//
   140		// Start always sends this value to CreateOrUpdateConsumer, so a nil also
   141		// CLEARS any ladder already on the durable. A consumer whose ladder is
   142		// managed declaratively therefore cannot just omit it here — that erases
   143		// the managed ladder on every start. Declarative management needs a
   144		// bind-only mode that skips consumer creation, which does not exist yet;
   145		// until it does, the app states the ladder here.
   146		BackOff []time.Duration
   147	
   148		// Retry is where this consumer's retries END: dead-letter capture, then
   149		// settle, plus — when its RetryConfig names a FloorMonitor — the
   150		// experimental floor-age circuit breaker. It does NOT schedule
   151		// redelivery; BackOff above does. When set, [Process] dead-letters an
   152		// undecodable payload instead of Terming it, and the whole schedule
   153		// (ladder, AckWait, MaxDeliver, and this Retry's expectations of them) is
   154		// validated together at Start. Its MaxDeliver must equal
   155		// EffectiveMaxDeliver().
   156		//
   157		// Handlers reach it through the closure they build, and call
   158		// [Retry.Settle] as their one disposition for a failed delivery. Nil
   159		// leaves disposition entirely to the handler, as before.
   160		Retry *Retry
   161	
   162		// FloorMonitor runs the durable's ack-floor health signal: [Start] polls
   163		// it and [Runner.Stop] joins that poll. Set it to publish the stall as a
   164		// gauge, or to drive a quarantine rule of your own, without adopting the
   165		// library's automatic breaker.
   166		//
   167		// Leave it nil when Retry already carries the monitor — Start uses that
   168		// one. Naming two different monitors is a Start error: one durable has one
   169		// ack floor, and one poll loop should read it.
   170		FloorMonitor *FloorMonitor
   171	
   172		// Tracer opens the per-message consumer span; nil uses the global OTel
   173		// tracer provider.
   174		Tracer trace.Tracer
   175		// Logger receives the scaffold's own log lines (decode-term warnings,
   176		// consume errors); nil uses slog.Default.
   177		Logger *slog.Logger
   178	
   179		// KeepInProgress runs a natsmsg.KeepInProgress heartbeat while handle
   180		// executes, for handlers that legitimately outrun AckWait. The extension
   181		// is capped, so a wedged handler still redelivers — see
   182		// natsmsg.KeepInProgress. The heartbeat stops when handle returns; a tick
   183		// racing the handler's own terminal Ack/Nak/Term is a client-side no-op
   184		// (nats.go marks the message disposed locally) that halts the heartbeat.
   185		//
   186		// Setting this forces the prefetch to one message (see MaxMessages): the
   187		// heartbeat extends only the delivery the handler holds, so anything
   188		// buffered behind a long handler would exhaust its AckWait unextended.
   189		KeepInProgress bool
   190	
   191		// MaxMessages caps how many deliveries the consume loop buffers
   192		// client-side (jetstream.PullMaxMessages); 0 uses the nats.go default
   193		// (500). AckWait runs from server delivery into that buffer, not from
   194		// callback dispatch, and callbacks run serially — so a consumer whose
   195		// handler can approach AckWait should keep this small or queued
   196		// deliveries expire and redeliver concurrently to other replicas.
   197		// KeepInProgress forces it to 1; setting both to conflicting values is a
   198		// Start error.
   199		MaxMessages int
   200	}
   201	
   202	// EffectiveAckWait is the AckWait actually applied to the JetStream consumer:
   203	// Config.AckWait, or DefaultAckWait when zero. Use it — not the raw field —
   204	// anywhere the real value matters, e.g. wiring a natsmsg.KeepInProgress
   205	// heartbeat by hand (a zero ackWait there is a no-op).
   206	func (c Config) EffectiveAckWait() time.Duration {
   207		if c.AckWait == 0 {
   208			return DefaultAckWait
   209		}
   210		return c.AckWait
   211	}
   212	
   213	// EffectiveMaxDeliver is the MaxDeliver actually applied to the JetStream
   214	// consumer: Config.MaxDeliver, or DefaultMaxDeliver when zero. Use it — not
   215	// the raw field — when building a backoff.Policy for this consumer's
   216	// messages: the two packages read zero differently (here it means "default
   217	// to DefaultMaxDeliver"; on the policy it means unlimited redeliveries, the
   218	// jetstream.ConsumerConfig semantics), so passing a zero Config.MaxDeliver
   219	// through verbatim would make TermOnExhaustion never fire on the broker's
   220	// real final delivery and orphan work-queue messages (COR-762).

    89		// decommissioned durable stops pinning every message it would have
    90		// received, instead of holding them until the stream's MaxAge.

   539		}

   551			jetstream.JSErrCodeConsumerEmptyFilter,
   552			jetstream.JSErrCodeConsumerExists:

   443	// Start creates/updates the durable consumer on nc and begins delivering
   444	// messages to onMsg, returning a Runner that Stops when ctx is cancelled. The
   445	// stream must already exist (provisioned declaratively); callers whose cells
   446	// opt in per-stream gate Start behind that opt-in so a cell without the stream
   447	// doesn't error at CreateOrUpdateConsumer.
   448	//
   449	// Consume errors are logged at Warn, except a drain/close during shutdown —
   450	// both the core nats.go sentinels ([nuts.IsShutdownFetchErr]) and jetstream's
   451	// own connection-closed error — which is a clean exit rather than a fault.
   452	func Start(ctx context.Context, nc *nats.Conn, cfg Config, onMsg func(jetstream.Msg)) (*Runner, error) {
   453		if err := cfg.validate(nc, onMsg); err != nil {
   454			return nil, err
   455		}
   456		js, err := jetstream.New(nc)
   457		if err != nil {
   458			return nil, fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer(%s): jetstream.New: %w", cfg.Name, err)
   459		}
   460		if err := cfg.checkAgainstStream(ctx, js); err != nil {
   461			return nil, err
   462		}
   463		cons, err := js.CreateOrUpdateConsumer(ctx, cfg.Stream, jetstream.ConsumerConfig{
   464			Durable:           cfg.Durable,
   465			AckPolicy:         jetstream.AckExplicitPolicy,
   466			AckWait:           cfg.EffectiveAckWait(),
   467			MaxDeliver:        cfg.EffectiveMaxDeliver(),
   468			FilterSubject:     cfg.FilterSubject,
   469			FilterSubjects:    cfg.FilterSubjects,
   470			InactiveThreshold: cfg.InactiveThreshold,
   471			MaxAckPending:     cfg.MaxAckPending,
   472			// Always sent, so an update carries it — and so a nil CLEARS whatever
   473			// ladder the durable had, leaving AckWait as the schedule. That is
   474			// why a declaratively-managed ladder cannot simply be omitted here:
   475			// see Config.BackOff.
   476			BackOff: cfg.BackOff,
   477		})
   478		if err != nil {
   479			return nil, fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer(%s): create consumer %s/%s: %w", cfg.Name, cfg.Stream, cfg.Durable, err)
   480		}
   481		consumeOpts := []jetstream.PullConsumeOpt{jetstream.ConsumeErrHandler(func(_ jetstream.ConsumeContext, cerr error) {
   482			if isShutdownConsumeErr(ctx, cerr) {
   483				return
   484			}
   485			cfg.logger().WarnContext(ctx, cfg.Name+": consume error", slog.Any("error", cerr))
   486		})}
   487		switch {
   488		case cfg.KeepInProgress:
   489			consumeOpts = append(consumeOpts, jetstream.PullMaxMessages(1))
   490		case cfg.MaxMessages > 0:
   491			consumeOpts = append(consumeOpts, jetstream.PullMaxMessages(cfg.MaxMessages))
   492		}
   493		cc, err := cons.Consume(onMsg, consumeOpts...)
   494		if err != nil {
   495			return nil, fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer(%s): consume %s: %w", cfg.Name, cfg.Stream, err)
   496		}
   497		watcherDone := make(chan struct{})
   498		r := &Runner{cc: cc, closed: cc.Closed(), watcherDone: watcherDone}
   499		if cfg.Retry != nil {
   500			cfg.Retry.attach(cfg.Name, cfg.logger())
   501		}
   502		if mon := cfg.floorMonitor(); mon != nil {
   503			mon.attach(cons, cfg.Name, cfg.logger())
   504			pollDone := make(chan struct{})
   505			r.pollDone = pollDone

   507				defer close(pollDone)
   508				mon.pollFloor(ctx, r.closed)
   509			}()
   510		}

   516			case <-r.closed:
   517			}
   518		}()

   520	}

   522	// isRetryableStartError classifies the narrow set of failures that can become
   523	// healthy without changing Config or replacing nc. Everything else returns to
   524	// the owner so a bad deployment cannot stay alive indefinitely with no
   525	// consumer. Unknown server-side 5xx responses are retried, except known
   526	// permanent JetStream configuration/account errors whose API happens to use a
   527	// 5xx status.
   528	func isRetryableStartError(err error) bool {
   529		if errors.Is(err, jetstream.ErrStreamNotFound) ||
   530			errors.Is(err, nats.ErrNoResponders) ||
   531			errors.Is(err, nats.ErrTimeout) ||
   532			errors.Is(err, nats.ErrDisconnected) {
   533			return true
   534		}
   535	
   536		var jsErr jetstream.JetStreamError
   537		if !errors.As(err, &jsErr) || jsErr.APIError() == nil {
   538			return false
   539		}
   540		apiErr := jsErr.APIError()
   541		switch apiErr.ErrorCode { //nolint:exhaustive // unrecognized 5xx codes are deliberately retryable; all other unknown codes fail closed
   542		case jetstream.JSErrCodeBadRequest,
   543			jetstream.JSErrCodeConsumerCreate,
   544			jetstream.JSErrCodeConsumerNameExists,
   545			jetstream.JSErrCodeMaximumConsumersLimit,
   546			jetstream.JSErrCodeJetStreamNotEnabledForAccount,
   547			jetstream.JSErrCodeJetStreamNotEnabled,
   548			jetstream.JSErrCodeConsumerAlreadyExists,
   549			jetstream.JSErrCodeDuplicateFilterSubjects,
   550			jetstream.JSErrCodeOverlappingFilterSubjects,
   551			jetstream.JSErrCodeConsumerEmptyFilter,
   552			jetstream.JSErrCodeConsumerExists:
   553			return false
   554		default:
   555			return apiErr.Code >= 500
   556		}
   557	}
   558	
   559	// Retry envelope for [Run]'s supervision: exponential from runRetryInitial
   560	// doubling to runRetryMax, reset once a consume loop survives longer than the
   561	// max. Package vars (not consts) so tests can compress the schedule.
   562	var (
   563		runRetryInitial = time.Second
   564		runRetryMax     = 30 * time.Second
   565	)
   566	
   567	// Run supervises the consume loop [Start] builds. Where Start is one-shot —
   568	// an error at consumer creation is returned, and a consume loop that closes
   569	// underneath the caller (consumer deleted on the server, subscription
   570	// invalidated) stays closed — Run retries both with exponential backoff
   571	// (runRetryInitial doubling to runRetryMax, reset after a loop that outlives
   572	// the max). In particular a stream that is not provisioned yet at boot — the
   573	// declarative-provisioning race — is a retry, not a crash.
   574	//
   575	// Run blocks until ctx is cancelled, then joins the live loop (including an
   576	// in-flight handler, see [Runner.Stop]) before returning, so it composes with
   577	// the cancel → join → drain shutdown ordering as the body of a supervised
   578	// goroutine:
   579	//
   580	//	g.Go(func(ctx context.Context) {
   581	//		if err := jsconsumer.Run(ctx, nc, cfg, onMsg); err != nil {
   582	//			log.Error("consumer config rejected", "error", err)
   583	//		}
   584	//	})
   585	//
   586	// Local configuration errors and permanent server responses (invalid consumer
   587	// configuration, authorization/account setup) can never succeed on retry and
   588	// are returned immediately. A missing declarative stream, temporary transport
   589	// failure, or unknown server-side 5xx response remains supervised. A nil return
   590	// means a clean, ctx-driven exit.
   591	func Run(ctx context.Context, nc *nats.Conn, cfg Config, onMsg func(jetstream.Msg)) error {
   592		if err := cfg.validate(nc, onMsg); err != nil {
   593			return err
   594		}
   595		delay := runRetryInitial
   596		for {
   597			// Each attempt gets a child context so the cancel-watcher goroutine
   598			// Start arms is released when the attempt dies, instead of one
   599			// accumulating per recreate for the life of the process.
   600			attemptCtx, cancelAttempt := context.WithCancel(ctx)
   601			r, err := Start(attemptCtx, nc, cfg, onMsg)
   602			if err != nil {
   603				cancelAttempt()
   604				if ctx.Err() != nil {
   605					return nil //nolint:nilerr // a Start error during shutdown is a clean, ctx-driven exit, not a fault to report
   606				}
   607				if !isRetryableStartError(err) {
   608					return err
   609				}
   610				cfg.logger().WarnContext(ctx, cfg.Name+": start consumer failed; retrying",
   611					slog.Any("error", err), slog.Duration("retry_in", delay))
   612			} else {
   613				started := time.Now()
   614				select {
   615				case <-ctx.Done():
   616					r.Stop()
   617					cancelAttempt()
   618					return nil
   619				case <-r.closed:
   620					// Join before recreating, not just cancel: the attempt's
   621					// ack-floor poll may still be in an in-flight consumer-info
   622					// request against the OLD consumer, and the next Start attaches
   623					// the same monitor to a new one. Without the join that reply
   624					// can land after the reattach and overwrite fresh state with
   625					// stale. Stop is cheap here — the loop has already closed.
   626					r.Stop()
   627					cancelAttempt()
   628					if ctx.Err() != nil {
   629						return nil //nolint:nilerr // the loop closing during shutdown is the expected wind-down, not a fault
   630					}
   631					// A loop that ran long enough to be called healthy earns a
   632					// fresh envelope; a flapping one keeps escalating.
   633					if time.Since(started) >= runRetryMax {
   634						delay = runRetryInitial
   635					}
   636					cfg.logger().WarnContext(ctx, cfg.Name+": consume loop closed; recreating",
   637						slog.Duration("retry_in", delay))
   638				}
   639			}
   640			select {
","process":"   640			select {
   641			case <-ctx.Done():
   642				return nil
   643			case <-time.After(delay):
   644			}
   645			delay = min(delay*2, runRetryMax)
   646		}
   647	}
   648	
   649	// Process runs the per-message prologue shared by every consumer: open the
   650	// consumer span (re-parented to the producer across the NATS hop), decode the
   651	// payload, and on a decode error record it, log "<Name>: decode <Stream>;
   652	// term", invoke onUndecodable (so the caller bumps its own drop metric with
   653	// its own attributes), and Term the message — a poison payload won't decode on
   654	// redelivery. On success it invokes handle with the span-enriched context, the
   655	// live span (for RecordError/SetStatus on the business error paths), the
   656	// message, and the decoded event; with Config.KeepInProgress set, an AckWait
   657	// heartbeat runs for the duration of handle.
   658	//
   659	// Callers wire Process as the func they pass to Start AND the entry point
   660	// their tests drive, so the decode-or-term path is exercised the same way in
   661	// production and tests.
   662	func Process[E any](
   663		ctx context.Context,
   664		msg jetstream.Msg,
   665		cfg Config,
   666		decode func([]byte) (E, error),
   667		handle func(ctx context.Context, span trace.Span, msg jetstream.Msg, ev E),
   668		onUndecodable func(ctx context.Context),
   669	) {
   670		ctx, span := natsmsg.StartConsumerSpan(ctx, cfg.tracer(), msg, cfg.SpanName)
   671		defer span.End()
   672	
   673		ev, err := decode(msg.Data())
   674		if err != nil {
   675			span.RecordError(err)
   676			span.SetStatus(codes.Error, "decode")
   677			disposition := "term"
   678			if cfg.Retry != nil {
   679				disposition = "dead-letter"
   680			}
   681			cfg.logger().WarnContext(ctx, cfg.Name+": decode "+cfg.Stream+"; "+disposition,
   682				slog.Any("error", err), slog.String("subject", msg.Subject()))
   683			if onUndecodable != nil {
   684				onUndecodable(ctx)
   685			}
   686			if cfg.Retry != nil {
   687				// Same terminal effect as the Term below, but the payload
   688				// survives: a bare Term settles the message perfectly well, it
   689				// just leaves no trace of what was discarded — the last
   690				// drop-without-a-record surface in this scaffold, and a Retry is
   691				// exactly the capture path that closes it.
   692				if _, dlErr := cfg.Retry.DeadLetter(ctx, msg, "undecodable: "+err.Error()); dlErr != nil {
   693					cfg.logger().WarnContext(ctx, cfg.Name+": dead-letter undecodable failed", slog.Any("error", dlErr))
   694				}
   695				return
   696			}
   697			if termErr := msg.Term(); termErr != nil {
   698				cfg.logger().WarnContext(ctx, cfg.Name+": term failed", slog.Any("error", termErr))
   699			}
   700			return
   701		}
   702		if cfg.KeepInProgress {
   703			stop := natsmsg.KeepInProgress(msg.InProgress, cfg.EffectiveAckWait())
   704			defer stop()
   705		}
   706		handle(ctx, span, msg, ev)
   707	}
"}

   223	func assertGap(t *testing.T, label string, observed, want, tolerance time.Duration) {
   224		t.Helper()
   225		delta := observed - want
   226		if delta < 0 {
   227			delta = -delta
   228		}
   229		if delta > tolerance {
   230			t.Errorf("%s came after %v, want %v ±%v", label, observed, want, tolerance)

   233	
   234	// TestLifecycleCleanFan_AdvancesTheAckFloor pins the success path against a real
   235	// broker: an Acked delivery settles, so the durable's ack floor moves and nothing
   236	// is left pending.
   237	//
   238	// The floor is the signal every stall alert on these streams reads, and it is the
   239	// one thing a fake cannot show — natsmsgtest.FakeMsg records that Ack was called,
   240	// never that the server accepted it. A denied $JS.ACK publish returns no error at
   241	// all (COR-1224), so "we called Ack" and "the message is settled" are genuinely
   242	// different claims.
   243	func TestLifecycleCleanFan_AdvancesTheAckFloor(t *testing.T) {
   244		t.Parallel()
   245		nc, js := natstest.Env(t, lifecycleTestStream())
   246	
   247		cfg := lifecycleConsumerConfig(lifecycleDurable, lifecycleSubjectFilter)
   248		cfg.AckWait = 2 * time.Second
   249		cfg.BackOff = []time.Duration{2 * time.Second}
   250		cfg.MaxDeliver = 3
   251	
   252		eu := &recordingJS{}
   253		c := &lifecycleConsumer{
   254			nc:      nc,
   255			fanout:  &lifecycleFanout{remotes: map[string]metajobs.JetStreamPublisher{"eu": eu}, localClusterID: "us"},
   256			durable: lifecycleDurable,
   257			subject: lifecycleSubjectFilter,
   258		}
   259	
   260		done := make(chan struct{}, 1)
   261		ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(t.Context())
   262		defer cancel()
   263		runner, err := jsconsumer.Start(ctx, nc, cfg, func(msg jetstream.Msg) {
   264			c.handle(ctx, cfg, msg)
   265			select {
   266			case done <- struct{}{}:
   267			default:
   268			}
   269		})
   270		if err != nil {
   271			t.Fatalf("start: %v", err)
   272		}
   273		defer runner.Stop()
   274	
   275		natstest.Publish(t, js, lifecycleStream+".github_handle.created", lifecycleBody)
   276		select {
   277		case <-done:
   278		case <-time.After(10 * time.Second):
   279			t.Fatal("the delivery never reached the handler")
   280		}
   281	
   282		stream, err := js.Stream(t.Context(), lifecycleStream)
   283		if err != nil {
   284			t.Fatalf("stream handle: %v", err)
   285		}
   286		cons, err := stream.Consumer(t.Context(), lifecycleDurable)
   287		if err != nil {
   288			t.Fatalf("consumer handle: %v", err)
   289		}
   290		// The ack is fire-and-forget, so poll rather than read once: a single read can
   291		// land between the handler returning and the server recording the ack.
   292		deadline := time.Now().Add(5 * time.Second)

   297			}

   301			}
   302			time.Sleep(20 * time.Millisecond)

   310	// TestLifecycleReadiness_FollowsTheDurable is the regression test for the
   311	// /readyz finding on trail #102.
   312	//
   313	// jsconsumer.Run retries every failure it can and returns only on a permanently
   314	// rejected config, so a readiness gate built on that alone stays green through the
   315	// outages it exists to report: a stream not provisioned yet, or a JetStream API
   316	// unreachable while the TCP connection is up. The pre-existing natsregions check
   317	// does not cover either (it asks IsConnected only), and in lifecycle-only mode this
   318	// consumer is the pod's SOLE gate — so green there hides a real outage.
   319	//
   320	// Both directions are asserted, because only one of them fails if the probe is
   321	// deleted: NotReady before the durable exists, Ready once it does.
   322	func TestLifecycleReadiness_FollowsTheDurable(t *testing.T) {
   323		t.Parallel()
   324		// A broker with NO stream: the declarative-provisioning race, and the case the
   325		// old `subscribed` bool reported and configRejected does not.
   326		nc, _ := natstest.Connect(t, natstest.Server(t))
   327		c := &lifecycleConsumer{
   328			nc:      nc,
   329			fanout:  &lifecycleFanout{remotes: map[string]metajobs.JetStreamPublisher{}, localClusterID: "us"},
   330			durable: lifecycleDurable,
   331			subject: lifecycleSubjectFilter,
   332		}
   333	
   334		if c.Ready() {
   335			t.Error("a consumer that has never probed must report NotReady")
   336		}
   337	
   338		cfg := lifecycleConsumerConfig(lifecycleDurable, lifecycleSubjectFilter)
   339		js := natstest.JetStream(t, nc)
   340	
   341		if c.durableReachable(t.Context(), js, cfg, true /* inStartupGrace */) {
   342			t.Error("the durable reported reachable with no stream provisioned")
   343		}
   344		c.durableBound.Store(c.durableReachable(t.Context(), js, cfg, true /* inStartupGrace */))
   345		if c.Ready() {
   346			t.Error("Ready() is true while the stream does not exist — this is the outage /readyz must surface")
   347		}
   348	
   349		// Provision the stream and the durable, exactly as the app would.
   350		natstest.Stream(t, js, lifecycleTestStream())
   351		runner, err := jsconsumer.Start(t.Context(), nc, cfg, func(jetstream.Msg) {})
   352		if err != nil {
   353			t.Fatalf("start: %v", err)
   354		}
   355		t.Cleanup(runner.Stop)
   356	
   357		if !c.durableReachable(t.Context(), js, cfg, true /* inStartupGrace */) {
   358			t.Fatal("the durable reported unreachable after it was created")
   359		}
   360		c.durableBound.Store(true)
   361		if !c.Ready() {
   362			t.Error("Ready() is false with a live durable and an accepted config")
   363		}

   365		// And a permanently rejected config still overrides a reachable durable.
   366		c.configRejected.Store(true)
   367		if c.Ready() {
   368			t.Error("Ready() must stay false once the configuration was rejected")
   369		}
   370	}

   372	// TestLifecycleReadiness_ProbeRunsUnderRun pins that Run actually starts the probe
   373	// and that it converges — the wiring, not just the helper. Without this, deleting
   374	// the goroutine from Run would leave every assertion above still passing.
   375	func TestLifecycleReadiness_ProbeRunsUnderRun(t *testing.T) {

   378		c := &lifecycleConsumer{
   379			nc:      nc,
   380			fanout:  &lifecycleFanout{remotes: map[string]metajobs.JetStreamPublisher{}, localClusterID: "us"},

   382			subject: lifecycleSubjectFilter,
   383		}
   384		_ = js

   386		ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(t.Context())
   387		done := make(chan struct{})
   388		go func() {
   389			defer close(done)
   390			c.Run(ctx)
   391		}()

   394		for !c.Ready() {
   395			if time.Now().After(deadline) {
   396				cancel()
   397				<-done
   398				t.Fatal("Ready() never became true under Run: the readiness probe is not wired")
   399			}
   400			time.Sleep(20 * time.Millisecond)
   401		}
   402	
   403		// Run must also join the probe on the way out, so no ConsumerInfo is in flight
   404		// on a connection the caller is about to drain.
   405		cancel()
   406		select {
   407		case <-done:
   408		case <-time.After(10 * time.Second):
   409			t.Fatal("Run did not return after its context was cancelled")
   410		}
   411	}

   413	// TestLifecycleRun_ReturnsOnRejectedConfig covers the path the probe-join defer
   414	// used to deadlock on (review finding on trail #102).

   416	// Two defers would run LIFO — join first, cancel second — and the probe exits only

   773	func captureLogs(t *testing.T, level slog.Level) *safeBuf {

   794			}

1	package main
     2	
     3	import (
     4		"testing"
     5		"time"
     6	
     7		"github.com/entirehq/mirror-pipeline/internal/timingcontract"
     8		"github.com/entireio/go-nuts/jsconsumer"
     9	)
    10	
    11	// stagingLifecycleMaxAge is the tightest retention any cell gives
    12	// resource_lifecycle_v1: the base stream CR sets 96h, and the staging overlays
    13	// trim it to 6h. The ladder is checked against the tight one, since a ladder that
    14	// outlives retention never reaches its own end — the message is discarded first.
    15	const stagingLifecycleMaxAge = 6 * time.Hour
    16	
    17	// TestLifecycleTimingContract validates the shipped schedule and renders the
    18	// before/after table this migration's trail carries.
    19	//
    20	// "Before" is the MEASURED durable, not the old constants read back: snapshots of
    21	// all seven cells (4 prod + 3 staging) on 2026-08-14 showed no server-side
    22	// backoff on this durable, so the effective ladder really was the client's flat
    23	// NakWithDelay — unlike webhook-forwarder and fanout, which turned out to carry an
    24	// undeclared 41h ladder (COR-1270). That is why loop 1 can claim an
    25	// envelope-preserving migration and loop 2 cannot.
    26	func TestLifecycleTimingContract(t *testing.T) {
    27		t.Parallel()
    28	
    29		before := timingcontract.Contract{
    30			Name: "before (client Nak, measured)",
    31			Schedule: jsconsumer.Schedule{
    32				NakDelay:     consumerFailureDelay,
    33				MaxDeliver:   consumerMaxDeliver,
    34				AckWait:      consumerAckWait,
    35				StreamMaxAge: stagingLifecycleMaxAge,
    36			},
    37		}
    38		after := timingcontract.Contract{
    39			Name:     "after (server ladder)",
    40			Schedule: lifecycleSchedule(),
    41		}
    42		after.Schedule.StreamMaxAge = stagingLifecycleMaxAge
    43	
    44		for _, c := range []timingcontract.Contract{before, after} {
    45			if err := c.Validate(); err != nil {
    46				t.Fatalf("%s: %v", c.Name, err)
    47			}
    48		}
    49	
    50		// The property loop 1 promises: the envelope does not move. Only ownership of
    51		// the schedule does.
    52		want := timingcontract.Envelope{
    53			DeadLetterDelivery: consumerMaxDeliver,
    54			TimeToDeadLetter:   time.Duration(consumerMaxDeliver-1) * consumerFailureDelay,
    55			LongestRung:        consumerFailureDelay,
    56		}
    57		for _, c := range []timingcontract.Contract{before, after} {
    58			if err := c.CheckEnvelope(want); err != nil {
    59				t.Error(err)
    60			}
    61		}
    62	
    63		t.Logf("lifecycle timing contract:\n%s", timingcontract.Markdown(before, after))
    64	}
    65	
    66	// TestLifecycleLadderRungsMatchMaxDeliver pins the rung count against the delivery
    67	// cap — the first of the "three MaxDeliver numbers must agree" (ENT-1601). The
    68	// third, a Retry's own MaxDeliver, does not exist for this consumer: it has no
    69	// Retry, because it has no DLQ to capture into.
    70	//
    71	// The server rejects len(BackOff) > MaxDeliver outright, so getting this wrong is
    72	// a startup failure rather than a silent one; the test exists so the derivation in
    73	// lifecycleBackOff cannot be replaced by a hand-written list that drifts.
    74	func TestLifecycleLadderRungsMatchMaxDeliver(t *testing.T) {
    75		t.Parallel()
    76		rungs := lifecycleBackOff()
    77		if len(rungs) != consumerMaxDeliver-1 {
    78			t.Errorf("ladder has %d rungs for MaxDeliver %d; want %d — one per redelivery",
    79				len(rungs), consumerMaxDeliver, consumerMaxDeliver-1)
    80		}
    81		for i, d := range rungs {
    82			if d != consumerFailureDelay {
    83				t.Errorf("rung %d = %v, want the flat %v", i, d, consumerFailureDelay)
    84			}
    85		}
    86		// AckWait must equal the first rung or the server stores the rung in its place
    87		// and the declared AckWait never runs (measured in
    88		// natstest.REDACTED).
    89		if consumerAckWait != rungs[0] {
    90			t.Errorf("AckWait %v disagrees with BackOff[0] %v", consumerAckWait, rungs[0])
    91		}
    92	}

const patch = "*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: /private/tmp/mirror-pipeline-pr246-worktree/cmd/meta-fanout/review_timing_probe_test.go
+package main
+
+import (
+	"testing"
+	"time"
+
+	"github.com/entirehq/mirror-pipeline/internal/natstest"
+	"github.com/entireio/go-nuts/jsconsumer"
+	"github.com/nats-io/nats.go/jetstream"
+)
+
+// Diagnostic only: compare the legacy post-handler NakWithDelay clock with the
+// migrated delivery-time server BackOff clock when the handler is not instant.
+func TestReviewProbe_ClientAndServerClocks(t *testing.T) {
+	nc, js := natstest.Env(t, lifecycleTestStream())
+
+	const (
+		rung = time.Second
+		work = 400 * time.Millisecond
+	)
+	type arrival struct {
+		delivery uint64
+		at       time.Time
+	}
+	oldArrivals := make(chan arrival, 2)
+	newArrivals := make(chan arrival, 2)
+
+	oldCfg := lifecycleConsumerConfig("review-old-clock", lifecycleSubjectFilter)
+	oldCfg.AckWait = rung
+	oldCfg.BackOff = nil
+	oldCfg.MaxDeliver = 2
+	oldCfg.Name = "review-old-clock"
+	oldRunner, err := jsconsumer.Start(t.Context(), nc, oldCfg, func(msg jetstream.Msg) {
+		meta, _ := msg.Metadata()
+		oldArrivals <- arrival{delivery: meta.NumDelivered, at: time.Now()}
+		if meta.NumDelivered == 1 {
+			time.Sleep(work)
+			_ = msg.NakWithDelay(rung)
+		} else {
+			_ = msg.Ack()
+		}
+	})
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	t.Cleanup(oldRunner.Stop)
+
+	newCfg := lifecycleConsumerConfig("review-new-clock", lifecycleSubjectFilter)
+	newCfg.AckWait = rung
+	newCfg.BackOff = []time.Duration{rung}
+	newCfg.MaxDeliver = 2
+	newCfg.Name = "review-new-clock"
+	newRunner, err := jsconsumer.Start(t.Context(), nc, newCfg, func(msg jetstream.Msg) {
+		meta, _ := msg.Metadata()
+		newArrivals <- arrival{delivery: meta.NumDelivered, at: time.Now()}
+		if meta.NumDelivered == 1 {
+			time.Sleep(work)
+			return // migrated path: server timeout owns redelivery
+		}
+		_ = msg.Ack()
+	})
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	t.Cleanup(newRunner.Stop)
+
+	natstest.Publish(t, js, lifecycleStream+".github_handle.created", lifecycleBody)
+
+	readGap := func(ch <-chan arrival) time.Duration {
+		t.Helper()
+		first := <-ch
+		second := <-ch
+		if first.delivery != 1 || second.delivery != 2 {
+			t.Fatalf("deliveries = %d, %d; want 1, 2", first.delivery, second.delivery)
+		}
+		return second.at.Sub(first.at)
+	}
+	oldGap := readGap(oldArrivals)
+	newGap := readGap(newArrivals)
+	t.Logf("legacy client gap=%v; migrated server gap=%v", oldGap, newGap)
+	if oldGap-newGap < work/2 {
+		t.Fatalf("expected the legacy post-handler delay to exceed the migrated delivery-time delay by about %v; old=%v new=%v", work, oldGap, newGap)
+	}
+}
*** End Patch";
text(await tools.apply_patch(patch));

    46	// IsTransientFetchErr reports whether a pull-consumer Fetch or subscribe error
    47	// is a recoverable interruption — a dropped link, a drained connection, a
    48	// consumer that moved or was recreated — rather than a fault. It is
    49	// independent of shutdown: a NATS server rolling underneath a healthy caller
    50	// produces these while ctx is still live.
    51	//
    52	// Callers should log these below error level. The distinction that matters for
    53	// alerting is not "did a fetch fail" but "did it stop recovering", and a single
    54	// interrupted fetch cannot answer that.
    55	//
    56	// nats.ErrTimeout and context.DeadlineExceeded are deliberately absent, and
    57	// the reason is fetch-path-specific: an idle poll reaching MaxWait is the
    58	// steady state of a quiet consumer, and a fetch deadline can be a wedged
    59	// server as easily as a slow one. On a subscribe/create retry path the same
    60	// timeout usually IS deploy churn (a slow JetStream API during an upgrade),
    61	// but this predicate cannot see which path it is on — callers that retry
    62	// subscription setup must classify timeouts themselves.
    63	func IsTransientFetchErr(err error) bool {
    64		if err == nil {
    65			return false
    66		}
    67		for _, target := range transientFetchErrs {
    68			if errors.Is(err, target) {
    69				return true
    70			}
    71		}
    72		return false
    73	}
    74	
    75	// IsTransientSubscribeErr reports whether a subscribe/create retry error is a
    76	// recoverable interruption. It is a superset of [IsTransientFetchErr]: a
    77	// retried subscribe also absorbs the stream not existing yet (rollout
    78	// ordering, where the consumer comes up before the service that ensures the
    79	// stream) and a JetStream API slow to answer the consumer-info/create request
    80	// (nats.ErrTimeout / context.DeadlineExceeded — deploy churn on this path,
    81	// unlike a fetch, where a timeout is an idle poll and a deadline can be a
    82	// wedged server).
    83	//
    84	// Keeping the set here rather than in each caller is the point: two services
    85	// already share these consumer loops, and the alert noise this package exists
    86	// to remove comes back the moment their classifications drift.
    87	func IsTransientSubscribeErr(err error) bool {
    88		return IsTransientFetchErr(err) ||

    90			errors.Is(err, nats.ErrTimeout) ||
    91			errors.Is(err, context.DeadlineExceeded)

1	// Package timingcontract states a consume loop's redelivery timing as data, and
     2	// checks it with go-nuts' exported arithmetic rather than by hand.
     3	//
     4	// # Why the arithmetic is not restated here
     5	//
     6	// ENT-1535 was a consumer whose real redelivery envelope was 34h22m while its
     7	// config advertised 17h45m, and duplicated timing arithmetic is exactly how that
     8	// happens: one number in a comment, another in a config, a third in a runbook,
     9	// and nothing forcing them to agree. [jsconsumer.Schedule] is the single
    10	// implementation — the same function go-nuts runs at consumer construction and
    11	// fleet CI runs over a rendered Consumer CR — so everything below delegates to
    12	// it and adds only a name and a renderer.
    13	//
    14	// A loop states its contract once, next to the constants it is derived from, and
    15	// its test calls [Contract.Validate]. Two loops in this repo cannot be validated
    16	// by jsconsumer.Start itself — cmd/worker and the meta-fanout lifecycle fan carry
    17	// neither a server ladder nor a Retry, so Start's schedule check does not run for
    18	// them — which is precisely why the check has to be reachable from a test.
    19	//
    20	// # The table is generated, not typed
    21	//
    22	// Every Track D migration trail carries a before/after timing table: the old
    23	// effective ladder against the new one. [Markdown] renders it from the same
    24	// Schedule values the test validates, so the table in the trail body cannot drift
    25	// from the ladder in the code. Print it from a test and paste the output.
    26	//
    27	// This package is deliberately pure: no testing import, no NATS connection, no
    28	// clock. It is safe to reference from production code — though today nothing
    29	// does, and a loop that wants its contract at runtime should prefer failing at
    30	// startup through jsconsumer.Start.
    31	package timingcontract
    32	
    33	import (
    34		"fmt"
    35		"strings"
    36		"time"
    37	
    38		"github.com/entireio/go-nuts/jsconsumer"
    39	)
    40	
    41	// Contract is one consumer's redelivery timing, named so a violation and a table
    42	// row say which loop they are about.
    43	type Contract struct {
    44		// Name identifies the loop — the durable is the clearest choice, since that
    45		// is what an operator reads in consumer info and in a KEDA scaler.
    46		Name string
    47		// Schedule is the timing itself. Populate it from the loop's real constants,
    48		// never from literals retyped alongside them: a contract that drifts from the
    49		// code it describes is the defect this package exists to prevent.
    50		Schedule jsconsumer.Schedule
    51	}
    52	
    53	// Validate reports every way the contract does not hang together, or nil when it
    54	// is coherent. The violations come from [jsconsumer.Schedule.Validate]; only the
    55	// name is added.
    56	func (c Contract) Validate() error {
    57		if err := c.Schedule.Err(); err != nil {
    58			return fmt.Errorf("%s: %w", c.Name, err)
    59		}
    60		return nil
    61	}
    62

    64	// non-positive MaxDeliver, matching jetstream.ConsumerConfig and

   174				fmt.Fprintf(&b, "- **%s** — unlimited redeliveries: no terminal branch, so no envelope to table.\n", c.Name)
   175				continue
   176			}
   177			e := c.Envelope()
   178			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "- **%s** — gives up on delivery %d at %s; longest rung %s",
   179				c.Name, e.DeadLetterDelivery, e.TimeToDeadLetter, e.LongestRung)
   180			if c.Schedule.StreamMaxAge > 0 {
   181				fmt.Fprintf(&b, "; stream discards after %s", c.Schedule.StreamMaxAge)
   182			}
   183			b.WriteString(".\n")
   184		}
   185		return b.String()
   186	}
   187	
   188	// cell renders one contract's entry for delivery n: when it arrives, and what
   189	// happens on it. A delivery past this contract's cap is blank rather than zero —
   190	// the two schedules being compared often have different caps, and a "0s" there
   191	// reads as an instant retry.
   192	func cell(c Contract, n int) string {
   193		if c.Schedule.MaxDeliver > 0 && n > c.Schedule.MaxDeliver {
   194			return ""
   195		}
   196		at := "t+" + c.Schedule.CumulativeTo(n).String()
   197		switch {
   198		case n == c.Schedule.DeadLetterDelivery():
   199			return at + " — give up"
   200		case c.Schedule.RecoverBy > 0 && n == c.Schedule.RecoverBy:
   201			return at + " — RecoverBy"
   202		case c.Schedule.MaxDeliver > 0 && n > c.Schedule.DeadLetterDelivery():
   203			return at + " — capture reserve"
   204		default:
   205			return at
   206		}
   207	}

1	// Package timingcontract states a consume loop's redelivery timing as data, and
     2	// checks it with go-nuts' exported arithmetic rather than by hand.
     3	//
     4	// # Why the arithmetic is not restated here
     5	//
     6	// ENT-1535 was a consumer whose real redelivery envelope was 34h22m while its
     7	// config advertised 17h45m, and duplicated timing arithmetic is exactly how that
     8	// happens: one number in a comment, another in a config, a third in a runbook,
     9	// and nothing forcing them to agree. [jsconsumer.Schedule] is the single
    10	// implementation — the same function go-nuts runs at consumer construction and
    11	// fleet CI runs over a rendered Consumer CR — so everything below delegates to
    12	// it and adds only a name and a renderer.
    13	//
    14	// A loop states its contract once, next to the constants it is derived from, and
    15	// its test calls [Contract.Validate]. Two loops in this repo cannot be validated
    16	// by jsconsumer.Start itself — cmd/worker and the meta-fanout lifecycle fan carry
    17	// neither a server ladder nor a Retry, so Start's schedule check does not run for
    18	// them — which is precisely why the check has to be reachable from a test.
    19	//
    20	// # The table is generated, not typed
    21	//
    22	// Every Track D migration trail carries a before/after timing table: the old
    23	// effective ladder against the new one. [Markdown] renders it from the same
    24	// Schedule values the test validates, so the table in the trail body cannot drift
    25	// from the ladder in the code. Print it from a test and paste the output.
    26	//
    27	// This package is deliberately pure: no testing import, no NATS connection, no
    28	// clock. It is safe to reference from production code — though today nothing
    29	// does, and a loop that wants its contract at runtime should prefer failing at
    30	// startup through jsconsumer.Start.
    31	package timingcontract
    32	
    33	import (
    34		"fmt"
    35		"strings"
    36		"time"
    37	
    38		"github.com/entireio/go-nuts/jsconsumer"
    39	)
    40	
    41	// Contract is one consumer's redelivery timing, named so a violation and a table
    42	// row say which loop they are about.
    43	type Contract struct {
    44		// Name identifies the loop — the durable is the clearest choice, since that
    45		// is what an operator reads in consumer info and in a KEDA scaler.
    46		Name string
    47		// Schedule is the timing itself. Populate it from the loop's real constants,
    48		// never from literals retyped alongside them: a contract that drifts from the
    49		// code it describes is the defect this package exists to prevent.
    50		Schedule jsconsumer.Schedule
    51	}
    52	
    53	// Validate reports every way the contract does not hang together, or nil when it
    54	// is coherent. The violations come from [jsconsumer.Schedule.Validate]; only the
    55	// name is added.
    56	func (c Contract) Validate() error {
    57		if err := c.Schedule.Err(); err != nil {
    58			return fmt.Errorf("%s: %w", c.Name, err)
    59		}
    60		return nil
    61	}
    62	
    63	// Unbounded reports whether the consumer never stops redelivering — a
    64	// non-positive MaxDeliver, matching jetstream.ConsumerConfig and
    65	// [jsconsumer.UnlimitedMaxDeliver]. Such a contract has no terminal branch, so
    66	// [Contract.Envelope] and [Contract.CheckEnvelope] have nothing to describe and
    67	// [Markdown] gives it a note instead of a column.
    68	func (c Contract) Unbounded() bool { return c.Schedule.MaxDeliver <= 0 }
    69	
    70	// Envelope is the handful of derived numbers a trail, a runbook, and a monitor
    71	// all quote. Pin them in a test so a ladder change that moves any of them has to
    72	// move the documented value with it.
    73	//
    74	// Only meaningful when [Contract.Unbounded] is false: an unbounded consumer has
    75	// no terminal delivery, so the derived numbers degenerate (a negative delivery
    76	// number and a zero duration) rather than describing anything.
    77	type Envelope struct {
    78		// DeadLetterDelivery is the delivery on which the terminal branch runs —
    79		// MaxDeliver less any capture reserve. For a loop with no Retry this is just
    80		// the delivery on which the loop gives up.
    81		DeadLetterDelivery int
    82		// TimeToDeadLetter is the cumulative SCHEDULED wait before that delivery.
    83		// Handler time and a lost delivery's AckWait sit on top of it, so a loop
    84		// whose handler runs for minutes has a real envelope far longer than this
    85		// number — cmd/worker is the worked example, and its own test pins the
    86		// wall-clock bound separately against the stream's max age.
    87		TimeToDeadLetter time.Duration
    88		// LongestRung is the largest single wait served before the terminal branch.
    89		LongestRung time.Duration
    90	}
    91	
    92	// Envelope computes the contract's derived numbers.
    93	func (c Contract) Envelope() Envelope {
    94		return Envelope{
    95			DeadLetterDelivery: c.Schedule.DeadLetterDelivery(),
    96			TimeToDeadLetter:   c.Schedule.TimeToDeadLetter(),
    97			LongestRung:        c.Schedule.LongestRung(),
    98		}
    99	}
   100	
   101	// CheckEnvelope reports how the contract's derived numbers differ from want, or
   102	// nil when they match. Use it to pin the figures a trail or a monitor quotes.
   103	func (c Contract) CheckEnvelope(want Envelope) error {
   104		got := c.Envelope()
   105		var diffs []string
   106		if got.DeadLetterDelivery != want.DeadLetterDelivery {
   107			diffs = append(diffs, fmt.Sprintf("dead-letter delivery %d, want %d", got.DeadLetterDelivery, want.DeadLetterDelivery))
   108		}
   109		if got.TimeToDeadLetter != want.TimeToDeadLetter {
   110			diffs = append(diffs, fmt.Sprintf("time to dead-letter %s, want %s", got.TimeToDeadLetter, want.TimeToDeadLetter))
   111		}
   112		if got.LongestRung != want.LongestRung {
   113			diffs = append(diffs, fmt.Sprintf("longest rung %s, want %s", got.LongestRung, want.LongestRung))
   114		}
   115		if len(diffs) == 0 {
   116			return nil
   117		}
   118		return fmt.Errorf("%s: %s", c.Name, strings.Join(diffs, "; "))

   120	
   121	// Markdown renders the delivery-by-delivery table a migration trail carries: one
   122	// row per delivery, one column per contract, each cell the cumulative scheduled
   123	// wait by which that delivery arrives. Pass the before and after contracts
   124	// together to get the comparison in a single table.

   127	// terminal delivery, so a cumulative table with a give-up row would be inventing
   128	// one. It gets a note instead, and the bounded contracts still table normally —
   129	// so a mixed before/after comparison reports honestly rather than summarising the
   130	// unbounded side as "gives up on delivery -1 at 0s".
   131	func Markdown(contracts ...Contract) string {
   132		if len(contracts) == 0 {
   133			return ""
   134		}
   135	
   136		var bounded []Contract
   137		rows := 0
   138		for _, c := range contracts {
   139			if c.Unbounded() {
   140				continue
   141			}
   142			bounded = append(bounded, c)
   143			if c.Schedule.MaxDeliver > rows {
   144				rows = c.Schedule.MaxDeliver
   145			}
   146		}

   148		var b strings.Builder
   149		if len(bounded) > 0 {

   153			}
   154			b.WriteString("\n|---:|")
   155			for range bounded {
   156				b.WriteString("---|")
   157			}
   158			b.WriteString("\n")

   161				fmt.Fprintf(&b, "| %d |", n)
   162				for _, c := range bounded {
   163					b.WriteString(" " + cell(c, n) + " |")
   164				}
   165				b.WriteString("\n")
   166			}
   167			b.WriteString("\n")
   168		}
   169	
   170		// Summaries follow the caller's order, so a before/after pair reads in the
   171		// order it was passed even when one side is unbounded.

   182			}

   184		}
   185		return b.String()
   186	}
