apiVersion: helm.toolkit.fluxcd.io/v2
kind: HelmRelease
metadata:
  name: nats
  namespace: nats
spec:
  interval: 30m
  chart:
    spec:
      chart: nats
      # Chart version == nats-server appVersion for this chart since 2.12.1, so
      # this line IS the server pin (there is no image override anywhere in
      # apps/nats). Rendered diff 2.14.2 -> 2.14.4 is exactly the image tag plus
      # the version labels — every new value the chart grew in between
      # (config.lameDuck*, container.*Probe, podTemplate.terminationGracePeriodSeconds)
      # defaults to the value that was previously hard-coded in the template.
      #
      # 2.14.4 (COR-1223, after INC-49) carries three fixes we want:
      #   - #8389 stream publish checks now include the filestore max message
      #     size, so an oversized record is rejected BEFORE proposal instead of
      #     reaching the filestore and latching fs.werr (the INC-49 wedge —
      #     see the max_payload note below, which stays as first-line defence).
      #   - #8378 a race between concurrent removals-via-limits could disable
      #     writes into a filestore. Same "stream silently stops accepting
      #     writes" outcome, different trigger, and NO payload cap protects
      #     against it — this is the fix that closes exposure we still carry.
      #   - raft proposals now carry the term down from JetStream, so a stale
      #     proposal from a previous term can't apply in a new one (the
      #     "replicas not becoming current" symptom during INC-49).
      #
      # ROLLING THIS IS THE RISKY PART, NOT THE VERSION. All 7 NATS clusters
      # share this file, so bumping it here would otherwise roll every cluster
      # (staging AND prod) within one 5m reconcile. The rollout is staged with
      # temporary hold-back pins in the per-cluster overlays — each pins
      # "2.14.2" and is removed one cluster at a time, quorum-checked between
      # clusters. See docs/runbooks/nats-server-upgrade.md.
      version: "2.14.4"
      sourceRef:
        kind: HelmRepository
        name: nats
        namespace: flux-system
  # Default Helm timeout is 5m, which is too tight for a 3-pod NATS
  # StatefulSet rolling restart (each pod replays the JetStream WAL and
  # has to re-establish cluster-route mTLS before becoming Ready). When
  # config changes land in quick succession, every reconcile rolls the
  # StatefulSet and times out — leaving the HelmRelease Stalled even
  # though the rollout completes asynchronously.
  #
  # 20m, not 10m (COR-1223): a *version* bump rolls all 3 pods for real,
  # unlike a config change (the reloader hot-reloads those without a
  # restart). Measured cost per pod is ~2m — up to 60s of lame-duck drain
  # (terminationGracePeriodSeconds) plus a fresh image pull and the
  # startupProbe's full /healthz, which does not pass until every stream
  # and consumer on that pod is current. ~6m for 3 pods left too little
  # headroom under 10m, and overrunning is not a benign "Stalled": with no
  # spec.upgrade.remediation set, helm-controller defaults to ROLLBACK,
  # which re-rolls all 3 pods back to the old image mid-flight. Keep this
  # matched with spec.timeout on each cluster's app-nats Kustomization,
  # which health-gates the same rollout (wait: true is patched in by the
  # cluster's apps/kustomization.yaml).
  upgrade:
    timeout: 20m
  values:
    config:
      cluster:
        enabled: true
        port: 6222
        replicas: 3
        routeURLs:
          # Build cluster route URLs as FQDN
          # (nats-N.nats-headless.<ns>.svc.cluster.local) so they match the
          # wildcard SAN on nats-server-tls (*.nats-headless.nats.svc.cluster.local).
          # Default `false` produces short-form URLs (nats-N.nats-headless)
          # which X.509 wildcard SANs don't match, breaking the cluster-route
          # TLS handshake with: "certificate is valid for ..., not nats-1.nats-headless".
          useFQDN: true
        tls:
          # Cluster-route mTLS — every pod-to-pod handshake on :6222 presents
          # nats-server-tls and verifies the peer against the same CA. The chart
          # auto-mounts the secret at config.cluster.tls.dir (default
          # /etc/nats-certs/cluster/) so no manual volume/mount is needed.
          #
          # Note: `verify: true` (mutual cert verification against the CA) is
          # sufficient for cluster routes — both ends are the same NATS server
          # presenting the same cert (CN=nats-server). We do NOT add
          # `verify_and_map: true` here because the CN doesn't map to a user
          # in authorization.users[]; route auth would fail with
          # "Authorization Violation". verify_and_map is correct on the client
          # listener (config.nats.tls.merge) where each client cert's DNS SAN
          # maps to a workload user.
          enabled: true
          secretName: nats-server-tls
          merge:
            verify: true
            ca_file: /etc/nats-certs/cluster/ca.crt
      jetstream:
        enabled: true
        fileStore:
          enabled: true
          dir: /data
          pvc:
            enabled: true
            # Per-replica disk for JetStream. Each NATS replica stores a
            # full copy of every stream, so size against the per-replica
            # stream contracts (mirror-pipeline webhooks_github_v1 5 GiB +
            # mirror_git_v1 1 GiB = 6 GiB) plus headroom for the unbounded
            # tlog stream, JetStream raft / consumer state, and ext4
            # overhead.
            #
            # This is the staging/default size. Prod overlays
            # (apps/nats/overlays/eks-prod-*) bump it to 1Ti.
            #
            # Bumping this value can't be a single Flux reconcile —
            # volumeClaimTemplates is immutable on a running StatefulSet,
            # and the STS controller does not reconcile PVC size against
            # the template. See docs/runbooks/statefulset-pvc-resize.md.
            size: 32Gi
            storageClassName: gp3
      nats:
        tls:
          # Client mTLS on :4222. Auto-mounted by the chart at
          # /etc/nats-certs/nats/. verify_and_map matches the cert's DNS SAN
          # against authorization.users[].user below — each client's
          # _lib/internal-tls cert carries its workload name as a DNS SAN
          # (e.g. "mirror-worker") and NATS walks the SAN list until it finds
          # a matching user.
          enabled: true
          secretName: nats-server-tls
          merge:
            verify: true
            verify_and_map: true
            ca_file: /etc/nats-certs/nats/ca.crt
      monitor:
        enabled: true
        port: 8222
      merge:
        # NATS server max_payload defaults to 1 MiB. webhook-ingest publishes
        # the full raw GitHub delivery to webhooks.github.v1.> (file-backed
        # webhooks_github_v1 stream), and large `push` payloads exceeded the
        # default — every one failed with "publish forwarded webhook: nats:
        # maximum payload exceeded", 500'd back to GitHub, and never entered
        # the mirror pipeline.
        #
        # HARD CEILING: max_payload must stay BELOW JetStream's filestore record
        # limit, rlBadThresh = 32 MiB (hard-coded in nats-server
        # server/filestore.go — NOT configurable). A record over that is
        # accepted by the publish check, replicated into the stream's raft log,
        # and then refused by the filestore, which latches fs.werr — a STICKY
        # error that fails every subsequent write of ANY size, survives pod
        # restarts, and is only cleared by rebuilding the raft group. That is a
        # permanent stream outage from one oversized message, not a rejected
        # publish. This is exactly what happened on 2026-07-29: a 25,983,093-byte
        # push base64'd to ~33.04 MiB, cleared max_payload at 40 MiB, exceeded
        # rlBadThresh, and wedged webhooks_github_v1 for 97 minutes (~43k GitHub
        # deliveries dropped, never redelivered).
        #
        # Sizing chain — every step must hold:
        #   webhookMaxBodySize (23 MiB, mirror-pipeline cmd/webhook-ingest/webhook.go)
        #     × 4/3 (webhookevents.Marshal JSON-encodes Body []byte, so Go
        #            base64s it: +33%) + envelope/headers
        #     = ~30.7 MiB  <  max_payload (31 MiB)  <  rlBadThresh (32 MiB)
        # Keeping max_payload under rlBadThresh means anything that somehow
        # clears the HTTP cap fails CLEANLY at publish ("nats: maximum payload
        # exceeded") → 500 → no filestore latch, no stream outage. Prefer a lost
        # delivery over a wedged stream. Value in bytes (integer for conf/JSON
        # parser safety).
        max_payload: 32505856
        authorization:
          users:
            - user: "entiredb"
              permissions:
                publish:
                  allow:
                    - "repo_refs_v1.>"
                    - "$JS.API.>"
                subscribe:
                  allow:
                    - "repo_refs_v1.>"
                    - "$JS.API.>"
                    - "_INBOX.>"
                allow_responses: true
            # mirror-worker — one user covers all regions; the cert's SPIFFE
            # URI path segment distinguishes which cluster the request came
            # from at the receiver side. NATS itself doesn't enforce region.
            # $JS.ACK.mirror_git_v1.> is an explicit publish grant for the
            # consumer's acks. allow_responses only covers a single reply
            # (max: 1) within ~2m of delivery — fine for short jobs, but the
            # bootstrap-fetch path (promoted 2026-06-01, main-42f36e6) runs
            # long git clones + in-process pack indexing and sends in-progress
            # ("working") acks during the job. The eventual ack then falls
            # outside that one-shot/expired grant, so NATS rejects it with a
            # Permissions Violation for Publish to $JS.ACK.mirror_git_v1.>.
            - user: "mirror-worker"
              permissions:
                publish:
                  allow:
                    - "mirror.>"
                    - "$JS.API.>"
                    - "$JS.ACK.mirror_git_v1.>"
                    # COR-617: on a terminal sync the worker publishes a
                    # mirror-completion onto the in-cell repo_ops_v1 bus as the
                    # mirror_done op. Scoped to that op (not the broader
                    # repo.ops.v1.> the teardown producers hold) — the worker has
                    # no business publishing teardowns.
                    - "repo.ops.v1.*.*.mirror_done"
                    # Mirror-sync failure index (KV_mirror_sync_failed): Put on
                    # terminal failure, Delete on heal. The KV bind (STREAM.INFO)
                    # and the clear-path direct Get ($JS.API.DIRECT.GET.*) are
                    # already covered by $JS.API.> above.
                    - "$KV.mirror_sync_failed.>"
                subscribe:
                  allow:
                    - "mirror.>"
                    - "$JS.API.>"
                    - "_INBOX.>"
                    # Crash/exhaustion backstop for the failure index: subscribe
                    # to mirror_git_v1's consumer advisories to catch terminal
                    # failures the in-process write path missed (pod crash).
                    - "$JS.EVENT.ADVISORY.CONSUMER.MAX_DELIVERIES.mirror_git_v1.>"
                    - "$JS.EVENT.ADVISORY.CONSUMER.MSG_TERMINATED.mirror_git_v1.>"
                allow_responses: true
            # mirror-rekicker — the failure-index re-kicker (mirror-pipeline PR 2,
            # cmd/rekicker). A per-cluster CronJob that lists KV_mirror_sync_failed
            # and republishes each stored job to the LOCAL mirror_git_v1 so stuck
            # repos re-drive and self-clear via the worker's success path. Kept a
            # SEPARATE identity from mirror-worker because its rights are a superset
            # the worker shouldn't carry (a job PRODUCER): the worker consumes
            # mirror_git_v1, the re-kicker publishes to it. Least-privilege vs the
            # worker — publish is scoped to mirror.git.v1.> (the worker has the
            # broader mirror.>), and it gets NO $KV write grant (it only reads the
            # index: Keys + Get, both via $JS.API.>). $JS.API.> also covers the KV
            # bind (STREAM.INFO), the Keys watch (CONSUMER.CREATE on
            # KV_mirror_sync_failed), and the direct Get; _INBOX.> receives the
            # request/reply + watch-consumer deliveries. DEPLOY-ORDER: this grant
            # must reach prod BEFORE the cmd/rekicker workload (PR 2b) connects, or
            # its publishes 401 until Flux reconciles.
            - user: "mirror-rekicker"
              permissions:
                publish:
                  allow:
                    - "mirror.git.v1.>"
                    - "$JS.API.>"
                subscribe:
                  allow:
                    - "_INBOX.>"
                allow_responses: true
            # mirrorctl — the operator CLI (cmd/mirror-pipeline-admin,
            # mirror-pipeline #150), run on-demand as a one-off Job
            # (apps/mirror-pipeline/mirrorctl) to inspect/replay the webhook
            # DLQ and the mirror-sync failure index. Higher-privilege than the
            # automated users because it MUTATES: replay captured webhooks (publish
            # webhooks.github.v1.>), re-kick stored jobs (publish mirror.git.v1.>),
            # and operator-delete failure-index entries (publish
            # $KV.mirror_sync_failed.> — the delete tombstone; note mirror-rekicker
            # above has NO $KV write). $JS.API.> covers the read plumbing, validated
            # empirically on NATS 2.14 against the real client: $JS.API.STREAM.NAMES
            # (DLQ subject->stream scan), $JS.API.DIRECT.GET.KV_mirror_sync_failed.>
            # (failindex get), $JS.API.CONSUMER.CREATE.* (KV Keys watch + DLQ
            # ordered-consumer scan), $JS.API.STREAM.MSG.GET.webhooks_github_dlq
            # (dlq get); _INBOX.> takes the request/reply + consumer deliveries. Can
            # be tightened from $JS.API.> to exactly that scoped set if least-privilege
            # is preferred. The DLQ + webhooks.github.v1.> grants are no-ops in EU
            # (those streams are US-only); the failure-index KV is per-cluster. Cert
            # DNS SAN "mirrorctl" is what verify_and_map keys on. DEPLOY-ORDER:
            # land this grant before the mirrorctl workload connects, or its ops
            # 401 until Flux reconciles.
            - user: "mirrorctl"
              permissions:
                publish:
                  allow:
                    - "webhooks.github.v1.>"
                    - "mirror.git.v1.>"
                    - "$KV.mirror_sync_failed.>"
                    - "$JS.API.>"
                subscribe:
                  allow:
                    - "_INBOX.>"
                allow_responses: true
            # natsctl — the ephemeral NATS inspection box (apps/natsctl;
            # launcher fleet mise-tasks/ops/natsctl). Runs the stock `nats`
            # CLI in a one-off Job to inspect ANY stream / consumer / KV in
            # the cell — the generic complement to mirrorctl's curated,
            # domain-aware verbs above. Read-only at the ACL — only JS-API
            # read verbs, wildcarded across streams; NO STREAM.CREATE/UPDATE/
            # DELETE, NO STREAM.MSG.DELETE, NO CONSUMER.DELETE, NO
            # DURABLE.CREATE, NO app-subject publish — with ONE deliberate
            # carve-out: STREAM.PURGE on the enumerated dead-letter capture
            # streams below, so an operator can drain a DLQ after triage
            # without the break-glass admin pod. A fat-fingered purge of any
            # OTHER stream still gets a permissions violation. Broader
            # mutations stay with mirrorctl (curated, dry-run-gated) or the
            # break-glass admin-pod procedure in
            # docs/operator-guide/nats-operations.md.
            #
            # CONSUMER.CREATE.> is the one nuanced grant: `nats stream view` /
            # `kv watch` need ephemeral ORDERED consumers (AckNone — reads
            # remove nothing on any retention). Unlike entire-mcp below (which
            # enumerates streams and withholds CREATE on workqueues), this is
            # wildcarded: on a covered workqueue stream the server itself
            # rejects overlapping consumers, so a worker's coverage can't be
            # stolen; the residual edge — hand-crafting an AckExplicit consumer
            # on an UNCOVERED workqueue subject and acking work away — is
            # accepted for this kubectl-RBAC-gated human tool, and is exactly
            # why unattended services get the enumerated pattern instead.
            #
            # allow_responses covers the flow-control/heartbeat replies an
            # ordered push consumer must send (reply-subject publishes), the
            # same empirically-validated scan path as mirrorctl — natsctl never
            # serves a request.
            - user: "natsctl"
              permissions:
                publish:
                  allow:
                    - "$JS.API.INFO" # account-level JetStream info
                    - "$JS.API.STREAM.NAMES"
                    - "$JS.API.STREAM.LIST"
                    # STREAM.INFO also serves `nats stream subjects`: the
                    # per-subject breakdown is the subjects_filter field on a
                    # STREAM.INFO request (paged via offset), not a separate
                    # JS-API endpoint — no extra grant exists or is needed.
                    - "$JS.API.STREAM.INFO.*"
                    - "$JS.API.STREAM.MSG.GET.*" # get by seq / last-by-subject
                    - "$JS.API.DIRECT.GET.>" # direct gets, incl. KV reads
                    - "$JS.API.CONSUMER.NAMES.*"
                    - "$JS.API.CONSUMER.LIST.*"
                    - "$JS.API.CONSUMER.INFO.>"
                    - "$JS.API.CONSUMER.CREATE.>" # ephemeral ordered consumers — see note above
                    - "$JS.API.CONSUMER.MSG.NEXT.>" # pull fetch for those consumers
                    # DLQ carve-out — the ONLY mutations this user has: purge
                    # (whole-stream or --subject-scoped) and per-message delete
                    # (nats stream rmm) on the dead-letter capture streams.
                    # Enumerated per stream (subject tokens can't express
                    # "ends in _dlq", and that's a feature: a new DLQ stream
                    # must be added here deliberately). The DLQs are terminal
                    # parking lots — limits retention, no consumers, age out at
                    # maxAge — so purging/pruning drops captured dead letters,
                    # never live work. webhooks_github_dlq captures are
                    # non-reconstructible originals: inspect and replay
                    # (mirrorctl webhooks dlq) before dropping. Deliberately NO
                    # replay here — re-publishing needs app-subject publish
                    # (job-injection capability); replay stays with the curated
                    # per-service tools (mirrorctl for the webhook DLQ).
                    #
                    # ci_webhooks_inbound_dlq_v1 is the one whose captures ARE
                    # reconstructible, for a window: its source stream
                    # (ci_webhooks_inbound_v1) is limits retention, so an Ack
                    # leaves the original in place for maxAge 96h, and the
                    # documented recovery re-reads the SOURCE — rename
                    # ENTIRE_CI_WEBHOOKS_INBOUND_DURABLE_NAME and a new durable
                    # replays the retained window. Inside 96h a purge here drops
                    # a copy; past it, the DLQ's 14d is the only record left, so
                    # read before dropping. Without this grant the depth monitor
                    # (infra datadog-ci-webhooks inbound_dlq_depth, fires on
                    # depth > 0) could not be cleared after triage and would sit
                    # red for the full 14d, which is how an alert gets ignored.
                    - "$JS.API.STREAM.PURGE.webhooks_github_dlq" # mirror-pipeline webhook DLQ (US cells)
                    - "$JS.API.STREAM.PURGE.repo_ops_dlq_v1" # entire-core repo-ops DLQ (every cell)
                    - "$JS.API.STREAM.PURGE.repo_jobs_dlq_v1" # entire-api job DLQ (every cell)
                    - "$JS.API.STREAM.PURGE.repo_refs_dlq_v1" # entire-search ref-event DLQ (every cell, ENT-1492)
                    - "$JS.API.STREAM.PURGE.ci_webhooks_inbound_dlq_v1" # entire-ci-webhooks inbound DLQ (staging-us-west-2 only, ENT-1436)
                    - "$JS.API.STREAM.MSG.DELETE.webhooks_github_dlq" # per-message prune (nats stream rmm)
                    - "$JS.API.STREAM.MSG.DELETE.repo_ops_dlq_v1"
                    - "$JS.API.STREAM.MSG.DELETE.repo_jobs_dlq_v1"
                    - "$JS.API.STREAM.MSG.DELETE.repo_refs_dlq_v1"
                    - "$JS.API.STREAM.MSG.DELETE.ci_webhooks_inbound_dlq_v1"
                subscribe:
                  allow:
                    - "_INBOX.>" # JS-API replies + ordered-consumer deliveries
                    # kv watch belt-and-braces. Watcher deliveries ride the
                    # ordered push consumer's _INBOX deliver subject (the
                    # $KV.<bucket>.> filter is server-side) — the same
                    # empirically-validated path mirrorctl's failindex
                    # Keys-watch uses with _INBOX.> alone — but entire-mcp's
                    # grant below carries the KV change subjects too, so match
                    # that precedent for any client that core-subscribes them.
                    # Subscribe-only: read either way.
                    - "$KV.>"
                allow_responses: true
            # entire-mcp — the operator MCP server's READ-ONLY mirror-pipeline
            # surface (apps/entire-mcp; staging-only today). Inspects the
            # mirror-sync failure index (KV_mirror_sync_failed), the three
            # pipeline DLQs (webhooks_github_dlq US-only; repo_jobs_dlq_v1 and
            # repo_ops_dlq_v1 per-cell), the meta-fanout backfill work-queues,
            # and — via metadata-only wildcards — any stream/consumer's health.
            # STRICTLY READ-ONLY, at natsctl READ parity: it never publishes app
            # subjects, and never deletes/purges. So unlike mirrorctl (broad
            # $JS.API.> + $KV/app publishes because it MUTATES —
            # replay/re-kick/delete), this user gets ONLY read JetStream-API
            # verbs — but read of EVERYTHING, like natsctl: metadata
            # (STREAM.LIST/INFO, CONSUMER.LIST/INFO), message bodies
            # (STREAM.MSG.GET, DIRECT.GET) and ordered AckNone scans
            # (CONSUMER.CREATE/MSG.NEXT) across any stream, plus the enumerated
            # KV/DLQ reads below. NO mutation: NO STREAM.CREATE/UPDATE/DELETE/
            # PURGE, NO STREAM.MSG.DELETE, NO CONSUMER.DELETE, NO app-subject
            # publish. (The DLQ-purge carve-out natsctl carries is NOT ported.)
            # The MCP client only ever creates ORDERED (AckNone) consumers, so
            # the CONSUMER.CREATE wildcard can't ack work off a workqueue.
            #
            # Cert DNS SAN "entire-mcp" (internal-tls component, SPIFFE_NAME
            # "entire-mcp") is what verify_and_map keys on. The SAN is identical
            # in every cell, so this one base user also admits the EU deployment
            # when it dials the US NATS cross-region for the US-only DLQ +
            # backfill reads. Inert in prod until entire-mcp gets prod overlays
            # (no entire-mcp leaf connects there yet), exactly like an unused
            # user — harmless.
            #
            # NOTE: the exact $JS.API.* subjects below mirror mirrorctl's
            # empirically-validated reads (NATS 2.14) for the failindex + DLQ,
            # plus StreamInfo/ConsumerInfo for backfill; they were NOT verified
            # against the entire-mcp client source. Validate in staging (watch
            # for "Permissions Violation" on the entire-mcp connection) and
            # tighten/extend before any prod rollout.
            #
            # No allow_responses: entire-mcp only ISSUES read RPCs and consumes
            # their _INBOX replies; it never serves a request it must reply to.
            - user: "entire-mcp"
              permissions:
                publish:
                  allow:
                    # failindex — KV_mirror_sync_failed Keys + Get (per-cluster
                    # KV, present in every cell via base):
                    - "$JS.API.STREAM.INFO.KV_mirror_sync_failed" # KV bind
                    - "$JS.API.DIRECT.GET.KV_mirror_sync_failed" # Get (KV AllowDirect)
                    - "$JS.API.CONSUMER.CREATE.KV_mirror_sync_failed.>" # Keys watch — ephemeral ordered consumer; KV is history=1, the read mutates no data
                    - "$JS.API.CONSUMER.MSG.NEXT.KV_mirror_sync_failed.>" # pull delivery if the watcher is a pull ordered consumer
                    # webhook DLQ — webhooks_github_dlq ordered-consumer read
                    # (US-only stream; these are no-ops in EU's local NATS):
                    - "$JS.API.STREAM.INFO.webhooks_github_dlq"
                    - "$JS.API.STREAM.NAMES" # DLQ subject->stream scan
                    - "$JS.API.STREAM.MSG.GET.webhooks_github_dlq" # get by seq
                    - "$JS.API.CONSUMER.CREATE.webhooks_github_dlq.>" # ordered consumer — limits retention, so acks never remove messages
                    - "$JS.API.CONSUMER.MSG.NEXT.webhooks_github_dlq.>" # pull fetch for the ordered consumer
                    # per-cell job DLQs — repo_jobs_dlq_v1 (entire-api job poison,
                    # COR-960) and repo_ops_dlq_v1 (entiredb repo-ops poison,
                    # COR-944). Both are `limits`-retention terminal parking lots
                    # provisioned in EVERY cell (apps/nats-streams/base), so — unlike
                    # the US-only webhook DLQ above — these grants are live in every
                    # cluster. Same READ-ONLY shape as the webhook DLQ: StreamInfo +
                    # MSG.GET (get by seq) + an ephemeral ordered consumer (AckNone;
                    # limits retention, so the scan removes nothing). NO STREAM.PURGE
                    # / STREAM.MSG.DELETE — this surface never mutates a DLQ (that
                    # carve-out is natsctl's, kubectl-gated). The MCP dlq_list/dlq_get
                    # tools (dlq=repo-jobs|repo-ops) read these.
                    - "$JS.API.STREAM.INFO.repo_jobs_dlq_v1"
                    - "$JS.API.STREAM.MSG.GET.repo_jobs_dlq_v1" # get by seq
                    - "$JS.API.CONSUMER.CREATE.repo_jobs_dlq_v1.>" # ordered consumer — limits retention, acks never remove
                    - "$JS.API.CONSUMER.MSG.NEXT.repo_jobs_dlq_v1.>" # pull fetch for the ordered consumer
                    - "$JS.API.STREAM.INFO.repo_ops_dlq_v1"
                    - "$JS.API.STREAM.MSG.GET.repo_ops_dlq_v1" # get by seq
                    - "$JS.API.CONSUMER.CREATE.repo_ops_dlq_v1.>" # ordered consumer — limits retention, acks never remove
                    - "$JS.API.CONSUMER.MSG.NEXT.repo_ops_dlq_v1.>" # pull fetch for the ordered consumer
                    # backfill — StreamInfo/ConsumerInfo ONLY. Deliberately NO
                    # CONSUMER.CREATE here: github_meta_backfill is a workqueue,
                    # where a draining consumer would ACK-REMOVE queued jobs —
                    # this surface must never consume work. github_pr_backfill is
                    # not yet provisioned in fleet (see apps/nats-streams); the
                    # grant is harmless until that stream exists.
                    - "$JS.API.STREAM.INFO.github_meta_backfill"
                    - "$JS.API.STREAM.INFO.github_pr_backfill"
                    - "$JS.API.CONSUMER.INFO.github_meta_backfill.>"
                    - "$JS.API.CONSUMER.INFO.github_pr_backfill.>"
                    # generic read across ANY stream — natsctl READ parity, for the
                    # inspection tools (stream_inspect / consumer_report) and the
                    # message-read tools (stream_peek / message_get). Three verb
                    # families, ALL read:
                    #   1. metadata — stream/consumer config, depth, ack-floor/lag.
                    #   2. message bodies — get by seq / last-by-subject, and direct
                    #      gets (incl. KV). This is how an operator reads a poison
                    #      message parked on a stream that has no DLQ.
                    #   3. ordered ephemeral consumers — the DeliverAll/AckNone scan
                    #      stream_peek drives. AckNone removes nothing on any
                    #      retention; the MCP client only ever creates ORDERED
                    #      consumers, so this can't ack work off a workqueue (the
                    #      residual edge the same grant carries for a raw human CLI).
                    # Still NO mutation anywhere: no STREAM.CREATE/UPDATE/DELETE/
                    # PURGE, no STREAM.MSG.DELETE, no CONSUMER.DELETE, no app-subject
                    # publish. The DLQ-purge carve-out natsctl carries is NOT ported.
                    - "$JS.API.STREAM.LIST" # StreamsInfo — list every stream with its info
                    - "$JS.API.STREAM.INFO.*" # StreamInfo for any stream (metadata + depth)
                    - "$JS.API.CONSUMER.LIST.*" # ConsumersInfo — a stream's consumers with info
                    - "$JS.API.CONSUMER.INFO.>" # ConsumerInfo for any stream/consumer (ack floor, lag)
                    - "$JS.API.STREAM.MSG.GET.*" # GetMsg / GetLastMsg — read a message body by seq/subject (message_get)
                    - "$JS.API.DIRECT.GET.>" # direct gets, incl. KV/AllowDirect streams
                    # `.>` not `.*` on both: CONSUMER.CREATE.<stream>[.<consumer>.<filter>]
                    # and CONSUMER.MSG.NEXT.<stream>.<consumer> are multi-token (matches natsctl).
                    - "$JS.API.CONSUMER.CREATE.>" # ordered ephemeral consumer for stream_peek (AckNone — reads remove nothing)
                    - "$JS.API.CONSUMER.MSG.NEXT.>" # pull delivery for that ordered consumer
                subscribe:
                  allow:
                    # JS-API replies + ordered/watch consumer deliveries.
                    - "_INBOX.>"
                    # KV watch values (read) — the failindex Keys/watch path.
                    - "$KV.mirror_sync_failed.>"
            # webhook-ingest — receives GitHub webhooks and writes raw
            # forwarded deliveries to webhooks.github.v1.>. After the
            # cmd/fanout split, webhook-ingest no longer publishes
            # mirror.> directly — that moved to the fanout user below.
            - user: "webhook-ingest"
              permissions:
                publish:
                  allow:
                    - "webhooks.>"
                    - "$JS.API.>"
                subscribe:
                  allow:
                    - "_INBOX.>"
                allow_responses: true
            # webhook-forwarder — consumes webhooks.> and POSTs each delivery to
            # entire-web. Publishes only to webhooks.github.dlq.> — capturing a
            # delivery it dead-letters (mirror-pipeline pkg/webhookdlq, gated on
            # ENTIRE_WEBHOOK_DLQ_ENABLED) onto the webhooks_github_dlq stream. The
            # pod-crash advisory backstop also SUBSCRIBES to this consumer's
            # webhooks_github_v1 advisories (below) to re-capture deliveries the
            # inline path missed; GetMsg's STREAM.MSG.GET PUBLISH is already covered
            # by $JS.API.> below.
            - user: "webhook-forwarder"
              permissions:
                publish:
                  allow:
                    - "webhooks.github.dlq.>"
                    - "$JS.API.>"
                    # Explicit ack grant for this user's webhooks_github_v1 pull
                    # consumer. allow_responses below covers only ONE reply within
                    # ~2m of delivery, so an ack issued outside that window is
                    # rejected — "Publish Violation ... $JS.ACK.webhooks_github_v1.>"
                    # — and a rejected ack leaves the message unsettled, so it
                    # redelivers and the work repeats; on a poison message it pins
                    # the consumer's ack floor. A NATS pod restart is what reliably
                    # pushes acks past the window: this was observed on
                    # webhook-forwarder, core-fanout and fanout during the 2.14.4
                    # roll of eks-prod-us-east-2 (2026-08-10, COR-1223), and
                    # meta-fanout / trails-fanout carry the same latent gap.
                    # entire-core-global and entire-search already hold this grant
                    # for the same reason — this brings the remaining
                    # webhooks_github_v1 consumers in line.
                    - "$JS.ACK.webhooks_github_v1.>"
                subscribe:
                  allow:
                    - "webhooks.>"
                    - "_INBOX.>"
                    # Pod-crash advisory backstop (mirror-pipeline #159, COR-465):
                    # subscribe to webhooks_github_v1's consumer advisories so the
                    # backstop re-captures a delivery the inline DLQ path dropped
                    # uncaptured when a pod died between giving up and the capture
                    # publish. Wildcard over the durable token (mirrors mirror-worker
                    # above) — the workload subscribes only to its own
                    # WEBHOOK_FORWARDER_DURABLE; the wildcard just avoids coupling the
                    # grant to a durable name. The GetMsg refetch publishes to
                    # $JS.API.STREAM.MSG.GET.webhooks_github_v1, already covered by
                    # $JS.API.> above (the stream isn't AllowDirect).
                    - "$JS.EVENT.ADVISORY.CONSUMER.MAX_DELIVERIES.webhooks_github_v1.>"
                    - "$JS.EVENT.ADVISORY.CONSUMER.MSG_TERMINATED.webhooks_github_v1.>"
                allow_responses: true
            # fanout — pull-subscribes webhooks.> (US cells) and repo_refs_v1.>
            # (every cell, COR-1021: the native-mirror trigger consumer) and
            # publishes mirror.> sync jobs. Took over the mirror.> publish role
            # that webhook-ingest used to have before the cmd/fanout split. And
            # publishes webhooks.github.dlq.> — capturing a delivery it
            # dead-letters (mirror-pipeline pkg/webhookdlq, gated on
            # ENTIRE_WEBHOOK_DLQ_ENABLED) onto the webhooks_github_dlq stream.
            # The pod-crash advisory backstop also SUBSCRIBES to this consumer's
            # webhooks_github_v1 advisories (below) to re-capture deliveries the
            # inline path missed; GetMsg's STREAM.MSG.GET PUBLISH is already
            # covered by $JS.API.> below.
            #
            # repo.ops.v1.> teardown jobs are NOT published here: since COR-523
            # entire-core-global consumes webhooks_github_v1 directly and is the
            # producer of mirror teardowns (see the entire-core-global grant).
            - user: "fanout"
              permissions:
                publish:
                  allow:
                    - "mirror.>"
                    - "webhooks.github.dlq.>"
                    - "$JS.API.>"
                    # Ack/Nak for the native-mirror trigger's explicit-ack pull
                    # consumer on repo_refs_v1 (durable native-mirror-fanout) —
                    # same shape as mirror-worker's $JS.ACK.mirror_git_v1.>.
                    - "$JS.ACK.repo_refs_v1.>"
                    # Ack for its webhooks_github_v1 consumer (durable
                    # fanout-<region>) — see webhook-forwarder above for why
                    # allow_responses is not enough.
                    - "$JS.ACK.webhooks_github_v1.>"
                subscribe:
                  allow:
                    - "webhooks.>"
                    # Native-mirror trigger source stream (COR-1021): one ref
                    # event per committed ref change on repos hosted in this
                    # cell. Consumed in every cell — the home-cluster check in
                    # the binary decides which events fan out.
                    - "repo_refs_v1.>"
                    - "_INBOX.>"
                    # Pod-crash advisory backstop (mirror-pipeline #159, COR-465):
                    # subscribe to webhooks_github_v1's consumer advisories so the
                    # backstop re-captures a delivery the inline DLQ path dropped
                    # uncaptured when a pod died between giving up and the capture
                    # publish. Wildcard over the durable token (mirrors mirror-worker
                    # above) — the workload subscribes only to its own region-specific
                    # FANOUT_DURABLE; the wildcard just avoids coupling the grant to a
                    # per-region durable name. The GetMsg refetch publishes to
                    # $JS.API.STREAM.MSG.GET.webhooks_github_v1, already covered by
                    # $JS.API.> above (the stream isn't AllowDirect).
                    - "$JS.EVENT.ADVISORY.CONSUMER.MAX_DELIVERIES.webhooks_github_v1.>"
                    - "$JS.EVENT.ADVISORY.CONSUMER.MSG_TERMINATED.webhooks_github_v1.>"
                allow_responses: true
            # meta-fanout — consumes webhooks_github_v1 (star/fork/repository
            # events) on its own durable (a 2nd consumer alongside fanout) and
            # publishes per-placement github_meta.v1.<jur>.<cluster>
            # display-metadata plus github_pr.v1.<jur>.<cluster> pull-request
            # activity. Runs in US but cross-publishes github_meta.v1.> /
            # github_pr.v1.> into peer cells' NATS (EU/AP), so every cell's NATS
            # must authorize this identity to publish — hence base, not a US-only
            # overlay. Cert DNS SAN "meta-fanout" (internal-tls component,
            # SPIFFE_NAME "meta-fanout") is what verify_and_map keys on. Does NOT
            # publish mirror.> — that's fanout's git-sync output, not
            # meta-fanout's.
            # Also enqueues onto the dedicated github_meta_backfill work-queue:
            # the backfill one-shot JS-publishes jobs to github_meta_backfill.>
            # and the same identity's separate durable drains them via $JS.API.>.
            #
            # Also the cross-region fan-out for resource_lifecycle_v1:
            # subscribes the stream and re-publishes each event into every cell's
            # local stream (authorized in every cell via base) so each region's
            # entire-api consumes locally. Fan-out logic lives in the
            # mirror-pipeline binary.
            - user: "meta-fanout"
              permissions:
                publish:
                  allow:
                    - "github_meta.v1.>"
                    - "github_pr.v1.>"
                    - "github_meta_backfill.>"
                    # PR-backfill enqueue subject — sibling of github_meta_backfill
                    # for the `meta-fanout backfill-prs` one-shot (COR-683/COR-625).
                    # The draining durable uses $JS.API.> below, as meta does.
                    - "github_pr_backfill.>"
                    - "resource_lifecycle_v1.>"
                    # Ack for the explicit-ack pull consumer that drives the
                    # fan-out (nats.ManualAck + msg.Ack); allow_responses covers
                    # only a single reply.
                    - "$JS.ACK.resource_lifecycle_v1.>"
                    # Ack for its webhooks_github_v1 consumer (durable
                    # meta-fanout) — see webhook-forwarder above for why
                    # allow_responses is not enough.
                    - "$JS.ACK.webhooks_github_v1.>"
                    - "$JS.API.>"
                subscribe:
                  allow:
                    - "webhooks.>"
                    - "resource_lifecycle_v1.>"
                    - "_INBOX.>"
                allow_responses: true
            # core-fanout — consumes webhooks_github_v1 (push events) on
            # its own durable (a 3rd consumer alongside fanout / meta-fanout),
            # filters push, resolves a repo's placements via Core.RoutesForSource,
            # and publishes one deduped commit-author job into EACH placement's
            # local NATS island on github_push_author.v1.<jur>.<cluster>
            # (COR-757). Runs in US but cross-publishes github_push_author.v1.>
            # into peer cells' NATS (EU/AP), so every cell's NATS must authorize
            # this identity to publish — hence base, not a US-only overlay. Cert
