item.stdout:
a574849c1edc24a828dc0e31e1d53cfb39f8c889
test(meta-fanout): state the server retry clock honestly

Keep the lifecycle durable's server-owned 30s x 7 ladder and make the accepted clock-origin delta explicit: client NakWithDelay started after handler completion, while JetStream BackOff starts at delivery and overlaps handler work.

The shared timing renderer now labels its values as scheduled offsets rather than wall-clock guarantees. A slow failing publisher against the embedded broker proves the second delivery follows the server deadline, not handler duration plus the rung.

With the current three production remotes and a five-second publish timeout per remote, the legacy eighth delivery ranged from roughly 3m30s to 5m15s. The migrated scheduled eighth delivery is t+3m30s; no existing monitor or runbook encodes the older wall-clock range.

Gate: build, vet, go mod tidy -diff, git diff --check, gofmt, golangci-lint, go test ./..., and go test -race ./... all clean.
Entire-Checkpoint: 53ef0b702b0c

content.text: ok explain me this PR in simple terms, what's the problem, what's the solution
ok explain me this PR in simple terms, what's the problem, what's the solution

In simple terms, this PR standardizes how lifecycle events are copied between regions.

### The problem

`meta-fanout` reads lifecycle events from the local NATS stream and copies them to every other region.

Its consumer was hand-written:

- The application managed retries itself.
- NATS also had retry-related configuration.
- Those two sources of truth could disagree, producing surprising retry timing—the same class of problem that previously caused a 48-hour backlog.
- Consumer configuration was partly implicit and harder to test or inspect.
- Readiness and failure reporting were custom and inconsistent.

### The solution

The PR moves this loop onto the shared `go-nuts/jsconsumer` framework:

- NATS becomes the single owner of retry timing.
- A failed regional publish is left unacknowledged; NATS redelivers it.
- A successful fan-out is acknowledged.
- The policy remains eight attempts with 30-second scheduled intervals.
- The existing durable name is preserved, so its cursor and pending work are not recreated.
- The consumer configuration is explicit and tested against a real NATS server.
- Readiness now verifies that the durable is actually reachable.
- Existing failure telemetry and shutdown behavior are preserved.

One timing detail changes deliberately: previously, the 30-second delay started after processing finished. Now it starts when NATS delivers the message, so retries can happen slightly sooner. The PR now documents and tests that honestly.

In short: we replace a bespoke, drift-prone retry loop with one standardized consumer where NATS clearly owns retries and real-broker tests prove the behavior.

content.text:
The trails returned an issue: ```### Medium finding

**Location:** `cmd/meta-fanout/lifecycle.go:373`

Setting `BackOff` here means `jsconsumer.Config.validate`/`Start` now runs `checkAgainstStream`, which fetches `STREAM.INFO` for `resource_lifecycle_v1` on every (re)start attempt — a JetStream API call the pre-migration `PullSubscribe`-based consumer never made. If the meta-fanout NATS credentials in any of the seven cells weren't granted stream-read permission (only consumer create/ack was previously required), `jsconsumer.Run` will loop forever retrying a permission failure and this durable will never (re)create, silently keeping `/readyz` NotReady. The broker tests use an unrestricted embedded server so they can't catch a missing ACL grant — worth confirming the fleet ACLs for this consumer include `$JS.API.STREAM.INFO.resource_lifecycle_v1` (or wildcard) before rollout.```

# meta-fanout — consumes webhooks_github_v1 (star/fork/repository
            # events) on its own durable (a 2nd consumer alongside fanout) and
            # publishes per-placement github_meta.v1.<jur>.<cluster>
            # display-metadata plus github_pr.v1.<jur>.<cluster> pull-request
            # activity. Runs in US but cross-publishes github_meta.v1.> /
            # github_pr.v1.> into peer cells' NATS (EU/AP), so every cell's NATS
            # must authorize this identity to publish — hence base, not a US-only
            # overlay. Cert DNS SAN "meta-fanout" (internal-tls component,
            # SPIFFE_NAME "meta-fanout") is what verify_and_map keys on. Does NOT
            # publish mirror.> — that's fanout's git-sync output, not
            # meta-fanout's.
            # Also enqueues onto the dedicated github_meta_backfill work-queue:
            # the backfill one-shot JS-publishes jobs to github_meta_backfill.>
            # and the same identity's separate durable drains them via $JS.API.>.
            #
            # Also the cross-region fan-out for resource_lifecycle_v1:
            # subscribes the stream and re-publishes each event into every cell's
            # local stream (authorized in every cell via base) so each region's
            # entire-api consumes locally. Fan-out logic lives in the
            # mirror-pipeline binary.
            - user: "meta-fanout"
              permissions:
                publish:
                  allow:
                    - "github_meta.v1.>"
                    - "github_pr.v1.>"
                    - "github_meta_backfill.>"
                    # PR-backfill enqueue subject — sibling of github_meta_backfill
                    # for the `meta-fanout backfill-prs` one-shot (COR-683/COR-625).
                    # The draining durable uses $JS.API.> below, as meta does.
                    - "github_pr_backfill.>"
                    - "resource_lifecycle_v1.>"
                    # Ack for the explicit-ack pull consumer that drives the
                    # fan-out (nats.ManualAck + msg.Ack); allow_responses covers
                    # only a single reply.
                    - "$JS.ACK.resource_lifecycle_v1.>"
                    # Ack for its webhooks_github_v1 consumer (durable
                    # meta-fanout) — see webhook-forwarder above for why
                    # allow_responses is not enough.
                    - "$JS.ACK.webhooks_github_v1.>"
                    - "$JS.API.>"
                subscribe:
                  allow:
                    - "webhooks.>"
                    - "resource_lifecycle_v1.>"
                    - "_INBOX.>"
                allow_responses: true
            # core-fanout — consumes webhooks_github_v1 (push events) on
            # its own durable (a 3rd consumer alongside fanout / meta-fanout),
            # filters push, resolves a repo's placements via Core.RoutesForSource,

COR-1254 Track D — Consumer standardization: jsconsumer everywhere, durables as fleet Consumer CRs (wk 2–9, ~18 pd)

## Problem mirror-pipeline — the service whose whole job is consuming JetStream — has **zero** `jsconsumer` adopters; every fetch loop is hand-rolled. That's the failure class behind the 48h backlog (an app backoff config silently overriding AckWait) and it means no consumer inherits library fixes (circuit breaker, DLQ capture, telemetry). Consumer config is imperative, per-app, undiffable, and identical across cells whether that fits or not. ## Proposed solution * **Harden go-nuts first:** reject invalid configs at startup (backoff ladder > AckWait unrepresentable; DLQ policy required; no bare `Term()`); add bind-only mode (+ dev mode for local/CI); publish stream contracts as a module so `refevents`-style hand copies die. * **Migrate one loop at a time** ([COR-1009](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-1009/go-nuts-phase-5-migrate-remaining-consumeadmin-surfaces-to-the-modern) ph. 5): mirror-pipeline's 4 loops, then entiredb `permssweep`, entire-api `ingest`/`analysis`. * **Per loop, durables become fleet-managed NACK** `Consumer` **CRs** (extends nats-streams "Option A"): snapshot `nats consumer info -j`, author a full-mirror CR (`preventDelete: true`, explicit `ackPolicy`, `ackWait = backoff[0]`, live maxAckPending/maxWaiting stated), canary-adopt verifying ack floor/delivery counts unchanged, then switch the app to bind-only in the same change (single-writer rule). Go/no-go checkpoint after the first canary durable; fallback is app-owned consumers with library validation. * Durable advisory capture for the live index queue ([COR-997](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-997/durable-advisory-capture-for-job-stream-dead-lettering-close-the-repo)). **Exit:** 0 hand-rolled fetch loops; 0 app-side create/update calls; legacy consume-surface list empty; migrated durables are fleet CRs with delivery state untouched.

content.text:
This finding is resolved; no code or Fleet change is needed.

The concern is correct: `checkAgainstStream` requests:

`$JS.API.STREAM.INFO.resource_lifecycle_v1`

But Fleet’s shared `meta-fanout` identity already grants:

- Publish: `$JS.API.>`
- Subscribe: `_INBOX.>`

See [Fleet’s NATS configuration](https://github.com/entirehq/fleet/blob/2d975835df0fe7bd8d67b2bcf228416cb13d07e6/apps/nats/base/helmrelease.yaml#L626-L652).

That base configuration is used directly by all three staging cells, and I rendered all four production overlays to confirm they retain the same permissions. Therefore all seven cells can perform `STREAM.INFO` and receive its response.

It also would not fail silently: `jsconsumer.Run` logs every failed start attempt, `/readyz` stays false, and the lifecycle health supervision escalates after startup grace.

Verdict: valid dependency to verify, already satisfied. PR #246 remains unchanged and green at `a574849c`.

Setting `BackOff` here means `jsconsumer.Config.validate`/`Start` now runs `checkAgainstStream`, which fetches `STREAM.INFO` for `resource_lifecycle_v1` on every (re)start attempt — a JetStream API call the pre-migration `PullSubscribe`-based consumer never made. name: Promote image (nonprod → prod)

# Promotes one or more nonprod-ECR images to one or more prod ECR regions,
# then opens a single fleet PR that pins every target overlay to the
# resulting digests.
#
# Two ways to specify targets:
#   - prod_targets: JSON array of {overlay, region} objects — preferred for
#     multi-region apps. All targets land in one atomic PR.
#   - prod_overlay + prod_region: single-target shortcut (backward-compat for
#     single-region callers like sample, go-git-api).
#
# Two ways to specify images:
#   - image_name (+ optional image_key) alone: single-image promote,
#     backward-compatible with every existing caller.
#   - image_name + extra_images: promotes every image in one atomic PR
#     (one branch, one commit) — for apps that ship a sidecar built from the
#     same commit (see docs/developer-guide/multi-image-apps.md).

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      runner_provider:
        required: false
        type: string
        default: blacksmith
        description: "Runner provider (use github only as an outage fallback)"
      image_name:
        required: true
        type: string
        description: "ECR repo name, e.g. fleet/sample-app"
      image_key:
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ""
        description: >-
          The overlay's images[] entry to rewrite, matched on its `name:`
          field. Empty means rewrite images[0] positionally, the historical
          behaviour.
      extra_images:
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ""
        description: >-
          JSON array of ADDITIONAL images to promote and pin in the same
          fleet commit, e.g. [{"name": "fleet/librarian-ollama", "key":
          "ollama"}]. Each entry needs `name`; `key` has no fallback and is
          required once there is more than one image, or two would both
          rewrite images[0]. Promote builds nothing — every image here must
          already carry the tag being promoted in nonprod ECR.
      tag:
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ""
        description: >-
          Source tag in nonprod ECR, e.g. main-240d96e. Leave empty to
          auto-resolve to the most-recently-pushed `main-<sha>` tag for
          this image in nonprod ECR.
      prod_targets:
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ""
        description: >-
          JSON array of promote targets — preferred shape. Each entry:
          {"overlay": "apps/X/overlays/eks-prod-...", "region": "us-east-2"}.
          When set, all targets land in one atomic fleet PR. Mutually
          exclusive with prod_overlay.
      prod_overlay:
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ""
        description: >-
          Single-target shortcut (legacy). Path to one prod overlay.
          Region comes from prod_region (or aws_region fallback).
          Mutually exclusive with prod_targets.
      aws_region:
        required: false
        type: string
        default: "us-east-2"
        description: >-
          Default region for both nonprod (source) and prod (dest) ECR.
          Overridable per-side via nonprod_region (source) and the
          per-target region in prod_targets (or prod_region for the
          legacy single-target shape).
      nonprod_region:
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ""
        description: "Source nonprod ECR region. Defaults to aws_region when empty."
      prod_region:
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ""
        description: >-
          Destination prod ECR region for the legacy single-target
          shortcut. Ignored when prod_targets is set. Defaults to
          aws_region when empty.
      nonprod_account_id:
        required: false
        type: string
        default: "128096325110"
      prod_account_id:
        required: false
        type: string
        default: "934711778961"
      auto_merge:
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
        description: "When true, enable GitHub auto-merge on the resulting fleet PR."

permissions:
  id-token: write
  contents: read

jobs:
  # Split off tag resolution into its own job so the promote job's
  # `concurrency` key can reference the *resolved* tag via
  # `needs.resolve.outputs.tag`. Workflow-level `concurrency` only sees
  # `inputs.*` — with the auto-resolve default, two runs that resolve to
  # the same tag (one with `tag=""`, one with the explicit tag) would
  # otherwise land in different groups and race for the same branch/PR.
  resolve:

name: Promote image (nonprod → prod)

# Promotes one or more nonprod-ECR images to one or more prod ECR regions,
# then opens a single fleet PR that pins every target overlay to the
# resulting digests.
#
# Two ways to specify targets:
#   - prod_targets: JSON array of {overlay, region} objects — preferred for
#     multi-region apps. All targets land in one atomic PR.
#   - prod_overlay + prod_region: single-target shortcut (backward-compat for
#     single-region callers like sample, go-git-api).
#
# Two ways to specify images:
#   - image_name (+ optional image_key) alone: single-image promote,
#     backward-compatible with every existing caller.
#   - image_name + extra_images: promotes every image in one atomic PR
#     (one branch, one commit) — for apps that ship a sidecar built from the
#     same commit (see docs/developer-guide/multi-image-apps.md).

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      runner_provider:
        required: false
        type: string
        default: blacksmith
        description: "Runner provider (use github only as an outage fallback)"
      image_name:
        required: true
        type: string
        description: "ECR repo name, e.g. fleet/sample-app"
      image_key:
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ""
        description: >-
          The overlay's images[] entry to rewrite, matched on its `name:`
          field. Empty means rewrite images[0] positionally, the historical
          behaviour.
      extra_images:
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ""
        description: >-
          JSON array of ADDITIONAL images to promote and pin in the same
          fleet commit, e.g. [{"name": "fleet/librarian-ollama", "key":
          "ollama"}]. Each entry needs `name`; `key` has no fallback and is
          required once there is more than one image, or two would both
          rewrite images[0]. Promote builds nothing — every image here must
          already carry the tag being promoted in nonprod ECR.
      tag:
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ""
        description: >-
          Source tag in nonprod ECR, e.g. main-240d96e. Leave empty to
          auto-resolve to the most-recently-pushed `main-<sha>` tag for
          this image in nonprod ECR.
      prod_targets:
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ""
        description: >-
          JSON array of promote targets — preferred shape. Each entry:
          {"overlay": "apps/X/overlays/eks-prod-...", "region": "us-east-2"}.
          When set, all targets land in one atomic fleet PR. Mutually
          exclusive with prod_overlay.
      prod_overlay:
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ""
        description: >-
          Single-target shortcut (legacy). Path to one prod overlay.
          Region comes from prod_region (or aws_region fallback).
          Mutually exclusive with prod_targets.
      aws_region:
        required: false
        type: string
        default: "us-east-2"
        description: >-
          Default region for both nonprod (source) and prod (dest) ECR.
          Overridable per-side via nonprod_region (source) and the
          per-target region in prod_targets (or prod_region for the
          legacy single-target shape).
      nonprod_region:
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ""
        description: "Source nonprod ECR region. Defaults to aws_region when empty."
      prod_region:
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ""
        description: >-
          Destination prod ECR region for the legacy single-target
          shortcut. Ignored when prod_targets is set. Defaults to
          aws_region when empty.
      nonprod_account_id:
        required: false
        type: string
        default: "128096325110"
      prod_account_id:
        required: false
        type: string
        default: "934711778961"
      auto_merge:
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
        description: "When true, enable GitHub auto-merge on the resulting fleet PR."

permissions:
  id-token: write
  contents: read

jobs:
  # Split off tag resolution into its own job so the promote job's
  # `concurrency` key can reference the *resolved* tag via
  # `needs.resolve.outputs.tag`. Workflow-level `concurrency` only sees
  # `inputs.*` — with the auto-resolve default, two runs that resolve to
  # the same tag (one with `tag=""`, one with the explicit tag) would
  # otherwise land in different groups and race for the same branch/PR.
  resolve:
    runs-on: ${{ inputs.runner_provider == 'github' && 'ubuntu-24.04' || 'blacksmith-4vcpu-ubuntu-2404' }}
    outputs:
      tag: ${{ steps.source_tag.outputs.tag }}
      images: ${{ steps.normalize.outputs.images }}
    env:
      NONPROD_REGION: ${{ inputs.nonprod_region != '' && inputs.nonprod_region || inputs.aws_region }}
    steps:
      - name: Configure AWS credentials (nonprod)
        uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v6
        with:
          role-to-assume: arn:aws:iam::${{ inputs.nonprod_account_id }}:role/github-actions-ecr-push
          aws-region: ${{ env.NONPROD_REGION }}
          role-session-name: fleet-promote-resolve

      - name: Generate fleet deployer token
        id: fleet_token
        uses: actions/create-github-app-token@v3
        with:
          client-id: ${{ secrets.FLEET_DEPLOYER_CLIENT_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.FLEET_DEPLOYER_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          repositories: fleet

      - name: Checkout fleet scripts
        uses: actions/checkout@v6
        with:
          repository: entirehq/fleet
          token: ${{ steps.fleet_token.outputs.token }}
          sparse-checkout: scripts
          path: fleet

      # Validates image_name/extra_images (name charset, key whitespace,
      # duplicate name/key, "more than one image needs a key on every
      # entry") before the raw inputs.image_name interpolation below builds
      # an AWS CLI call with it — a malformed name should fail here with a
      # clear message, not surface as a confusing ECR error two steps down.
      - name: Normalize image list
        id: normalize
        working-directory: fleet
        env:
          EXTRA_IMAGES: ${{ inputs.extra_images }}
        run: |
          result=$(./scripts/fleet-images normalize --for promote \
            --name "${{ inputs.image_name }}" --key "${{ inputs.image_key }}" \
            --extra-images "$EXTRA_IMAGES")
          echo "images=$(echo "$result" | jq -c '.images')" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Resolve source tag
        id: source_tag
        env:
          INPUT_TAG: ${{ inputs.tag }}
        run: |
          set -o pipefail
          if [ -n "$INPUT_TAG" ]; then
            echo "Using explicit tag: $INPUT_TAG"
            echo "tag=$INPUT_TAG" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            exit 0
          fi
          # Empty tag → pick the most-recently-pushed `main-<sha>` tag in
          # nonprod ECR. Filter to `main-*` so feature/PR builds can't be
          # auto-promoted to prod; the rest of the workflow (and the
          # source-revision annotation) already assumes this shape.
          tag=$(aws ecr describe-images \
            --region "${NONPROD_REGION}" \
            --repository-name "${{ inputs.image_name }}" \
            --filter tagStatus=TAGGED \
            --output json \
            | jq -r '.imageDetails | sort_by(.imagePushedAt) | reverse | .[].imageTags[]?' \
            | grep -E '^main-[0-9a-fA-F]{7,40}$' \
            | head -1)
          if [ -z "$tag" ]; then
            echo "::error::No 'main-<sha>' tags found in nonprod ECR for '${{ inputs.image_name }}'. Specify tag explicitly."
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "Resolved latest main-* tag: $tag"
          echo "tag=$tag" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

  promote:
    needs: resolve
    runs-on: ${{ inputs.runner_provider == 'github' && 'ubuntu-24.04' || 'blacksmith-4vcpu-ubuntu-2404' }}
    environment: production
    concurrency:
      group: promote-${{ inputs.image_name }}-${{ needs.resolve.outputs.tag }}
      cancel-in-progress: false
    env:
      NONPROD_REGION: ${{ inputs.nonprod_region != '' && inputs.nonprod_region || inputs.aws_region }}
      NONPROD_REGISTRY: ${{ inputs.nonprod_account_id }}.dkr.ecr.${{ inputs.nonprod_region != '' && inputs.nonprod_region || inputs.aws_region }}.amazonaws.com
      PROD_REGISTRY_BASE: ${{ inputs.prod_account_id }}.dkr.ecr
      SOURCE_TAG: ${{ needs.resolve.outputs.tag }}
    steps:
      - name: Generate fleet deployer token
        id: fleet_token
        uses: actions/create-github-app-token@v3
        with:
          client-id: ${{ secrets.FLEET_DEPLOYER_CLIENT_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.FLEET_DEPLOYER_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          repositories: fleet

      - name: Checkout fleet repo
        uses: actions/checkout@v6
        with:
          repository: entirehq/fleet
          token: ${{ steps.fleet_token.outputs.token }}
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Compute image name list
        id: names
        env:
          IMAGES: ${{ needs.resolve.outputs.images }}
        run: |
          csv=$(echo "$IMAGES" | jq -r '[.[].name] | join(",")')
          echo "csv=$csv" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Normalize prod targets
        id: targets
        env:
          PROD_TARGETS_INPUT: ${{ inputs.prod_targets }}
          PROD_OVERLAY_INPUT: ${{ inputs.prod_overlay }}
          DEFAULT_PROD_REGION: ${{ inputs.prod_region != '' && inputs.prod_region || inputs.aws_region }}
        run: |
          if [ -n "$PROD_TARGETS_INPUT" ] && [ -n "$PROD_OVERLAY_INPUT" ]; then
            echo "::error::Cannot set both prod_targets and prod_overlay — pick one."
            exit 1
          fi
          if [ -z "$PROD_TARGETS_INPUT" ] && [ -z "$PROD_OVERLAY_INPUT" ]; then
            echo "::error::Must set prod_targets (JSON array) or prod_overlay (single path)."
            exit 1
          fi
          if [ -n "$PROD_TARGETS_INPUT" ]; then
            # Reject a non-array shape (e.g. a bare object) before anything
            # below assumes array semantics — jq 'length' returns 6 for a
            # string and 2 for a bare object, so the count check alone
            # doesn't catch either.
            if ! echo "$PROD_TARGETS_INPUT" | jq -e 'type == "array"' > /dev/null; then
              echo "::error::prod_targets must be a JSON array. Got: $PROD_TARGETS_INPUT"
              exit 1
            fi
            targets=$(echo "$PROD_TARGETS_INPUT" | jq -c '.')

        if: steps.ecr_check.outputs.exists == 'false' && inputs.runner_provider != 'github'
        uses: useblacksmith/build-push-action@v2
        with:

        uses: docker/build-push-action@v7

          build-args: |

content.text:
It’s not the whole AP South cell. The failure is isolated to its `meta-fanout` lifecycle consumer.

What happened:

1. Both new pods started successfully and connected to local and remote NATS.
2. During the rolling deployment, an old pod shut down. The legacy `PullSubscribe` client deletes the durable consumer when its connection drains.
3. The new pods noticed that first deletion and recreated the durable.
4. The second old pod then shut down and deleted the newly recreated durable again.
5. This time the new pull loops remained open but received only `no responders`/heartbeat errors. Because they never formally closed, the supervisor didn’t recreate the consumer.
6. The readiness probe correctly detected that `meta-fanout-lifecycle` no longer exists and marked both pods NotReady.

Current state:

- New image is deployed.
- Both processes are Running, with zero restarts.
- Both are `0/1 Ready`; deployment is `0/2 Available`.
- The lifecycle durable is still missing.
- AP South lifecycle events are therefore not being fanned to other regions. They remain in the local stream for its retention window, so this is currently a growing backlog rather than immediate loss.

AP South alone lost the timing race: its second legacy pod drained after the new durable had already been recreated. Other cells either completed both old-pod drains before their final recreation or otherwise avoided that ordering.

content.text: how do we fix it?
how do we fix it?

Two fixes: recover AP South now, then close the robustness gap.

Immediate recovery:

1. Recycle one of the two stuck AP South pods.
2. Wait for its replacement to create `meta-fanout-lifecycle`, become Ready, and process events.
3. Recycle the other original pod as well. This matters because it may appear Ready once its peer recreates the shared durable, while its own consume loop remains deaf.
4. Verify:

   - both original pod UIDs are gone;
   - deployment is `2/2 Available`;
   - the durable has the expected BackOff/MaxDeliver configuration;
   - backlog is processing;
   - no `consumer not found`, heartbeat, or `no responders` errors during the health window.

No legacy pods remain, so the durable should no longer be deleted during these restarts. I would not roll back—the old implementation is what deletes the durable during shutdown.

Permanent fix:

- Update `go-nuts/jsconsumer.Run` so `no responders` or heartbeat failures trigger a `ConsumerInfo` check. If the durable is missing, stop the stale consume context and recreate it instead of waiting forever for `Closed()`.
- Add a real-broker regression test with two runners where the durable is deleted twice—the second deletion occurring after the first recreation.
- Make readiness represent the local consume loop, not merely “some replica recreated the shared durable.”
- For future migrations from legacy `PullSubscribe`, use a two-release transition: first make the legacy client bind an explicitly managed durable, then migrate to `jsconsumer`. That prevents old pods from deleting shared state while draining.

The immediate recycle restores service; the library fix prevents this failure mode from recurring.

content.text: mmh is this going to happen every deploy?
mmh is this going to happen every deploy?

No—this specific failure is a one-time mixed-version migration race.

The old implementation owns the durable implicitly, so draining an old pod deletes it. The new implementation creates the durable explicitly and does not delete it when a pod shuts down. Once AP South’s two legacy pods are gone, normal new-version → new-version deployments should preserve the durable.

However, we exposed a separate robustness gap: if anything deletes the durable later—operator action, stream recreation, controller issue—the current consume loop may remain stuck instead of recreating it. That is not expected every deploy, but we should still fix it in `go-nuts`.

So:

- Recycle AP South now: resolves the one-time transition failure.
- Fix `jsconsumer.Run`: protects against future external durable deletion.
- Don’t roll back to the legacy version, or we reintroduce the delete-on-drain behavior.

mise-tasks/ops/natsctl-3-#
mise-tasks/ops/natsctl:4:# natsctl — thin launcher that runs the stock `nats` CLI in-cluster, on-demand,
mise-tasks/ops/natsctl:5:# under the least-privilege `natsctl` mTLS identity. It derives a one-off Job
mise-tasks/ops/natsctl:6:# from the suspended `natsctl` CronJob (fleet apps/natsctl — the GitOps-pinned
mise-tasks/ops/natsctl-7-# nats-box image + internal-tls cert + NATS env), injects your `nats` arguments,
mise-tasks/ops/natsctl-8-# streams the output, returns the exit code, and deletes the Job.
mise-tasks/ops/natsctl-9-#
mise-tasks/ops/natsctl:10:# Read-only BY CONSTRUCTION — with one carve-out: the natsctl NATS user
mise-tasks/ops/natsctl-11-# (apps/nats) is granted JetStream read verbs (STREAM/CONSUMER INFO/LIST/NAMES,
mise-tasks/ops/natsctl-12-# MSG.GET, DIRECT.GET, ephemeral ordered consumers) plus STREAM.PURGE and
mise-tasks/ops/natsctl-13-# per-message STREAM.MSG.DELETE on the enumerated dead-letter capture streams
mise-tasks/ops/natsctl-14-# (listed under NOTES in --help) so a triaged DLQ can
mise-tasks/ops/natsctl-15-# be drained or pruned without the break-glass admin pod. Every OTHER mutating

content.text:
{"id":"COR-1254","title":"Track D — Consumer standardization: jsconsumer everywhere, durables as fleet Consumer CRs (wk 2–9, ~18 pd)","description":"## Problem

mirror-pipeline — the service whose whole job is consuming JetStream — has **zero** `jsconsumer` adopters; every fetch loop is hand-rolled. That's the failure class behind the 48h backlog (an app backoff config silently overriding AckWait) and it means no consumer inherits library fixes (circuit breaker, DLQ capture, telemetry). Consumer config is imperative, per-app, undiffable, and identical across cells whether that fits or not.

## Proposed solution

* **Harden go-nuts first:** reject invalid configs at startup (backoff ladder > AckWait unrepresentable; DLQ policy required; no bare `Term()`); add bind-only mode (+ dev mode for local/CI); publish stream contracts as a module so `refevents`-style hand copies die.
* **Migrate one loop at a time** (<issue id="e9af1b79-ed6c-49fc-99c6-b90d4bc6f045" href="https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-1009/go-nuts-phase-5-migrate-remaining-consumeadmin-surfaces-to-the-modern">COR-1009</issue> ph. 5): mirror-pipeline's 4 loops, then entiredb `permssweep`, entire-api `ingest`/`analysis`.
* **Per loop, durables become fleet-managed NACK** `Consumer` **CRs** (extends nats-streams "Option A"): snapshot `nats consumer info -j`, author a full-mirror CR (`preventDelete: true`, explicit `ackPolicy`, `ackWait = backoff[0]`, live maxAckPending/maxWaiting stated), canary-adopt verifying ack floor/delivery counts unchanged, then switch the app to bind-only in the same change (single-writer rule). Go/no-go checkpoint after the first canary durable; fallback is app-owned consumers with library validation.

{"id":"COR-1252","title":"NATS robustness & standardization: stop fixing per-app, enforce per-layer","description":"## Problem

Every NATS correctness fix this month landed in the app where it bit, and the bug class resurfaced in the next app: Term-without-settle was fixed three times (<issue id="96688401-2b2d-48dd-8a77-a4400bd1bb45" href="https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/ENT-1492/entire-search-exhausted-ref-events-are-termed-which-does-not-settle">ENT-1492</issue> → <issue id="61e680fd-b8da-4226-8d21-e703b0482d29" href="https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/ENT-1525/ci-webhooks-the-outbound-dispatcher-still-terms-poison-ref-events-on">ENT-1525</issue> → <issue id="2e3ba22f-563d-407f-a1c0-28e470b8fe06" href="https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/ENT-1496/entire-search-lifecycle-consumer-still-terms-exhausted-events-same-ent">ENT-1496</issue> still open); five consumers were missing `$JS.ACK` grants (<issue id="33e005d5-f925-4d4a-b46c-d423ec5ac549" href="https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-1224/five-webhooks-github-v1-consumers-lack-an-explicit-dollarjsack-publish">COR-1224</issue>); an app backoff config silently overriding AckWait caused a 48h indexer backlog. The Aug 5–6 P1s (12 auto-incidents, one 9h ack-floor stall cleared with a lossy `stream rmm`) showed the new DLQ doesn't prevent stalls. Detection today is production P1s. NATS correctness lives in per-app convention — whack-a-mole.

## Proposed solution

Move every invariant into a layer where divergence is structurally impossible or automatically visible:

1. **Library owns the discipline** — floor-age circuit breaker + invariant-rejecting configs in go-nuts `jsconsumer`; apps inherit via migration.
2. **Config is generated, not hand-written** — durables become fleet-managed NACK `Consumer` CRs (extending the nats-streams "Option A" decision); NATS users, grants, and per-durable ack-floor monitors generated from the CRs; stream contracts published as a module.
3. **Admission control** — CR safety lint + import-boundary lint (raw JetStream calls legal only inside go-nuts, ratcheted).
4. **Continuous verification** — weekly poison-message conformance canary; NATS as a chaos fault target.

Four tracks as sub-issues, ~60 pd total, target Oct 30. Milestones: **M1** stalls dead (Aug 22) · **M2** routing real (Sep 5) · **M3** loops retired (Oct 14) · **M4** guarded (Oct 30).

{"comments":[{"id":"c459872d-079d-43a9-80c0-84112a0f6f88","body":"**Migration kickoff approved (2026-08-14, Andrea, after orchestrator review of the phase-0 analysis).** Full phase-0 read-out: 4 loops resolve to **11 durables ≈ 12 PRs**, one trail per consumer; Retry/DLQ adoption on exactly the 5 durables where DLQ + grant + enablement pre-exist; the other 6 keep designed give-ups (KV fail-index + rekick, workqueue TermOnExhaustion, retention-backed silent drop). Order: PR-0 (go-nuts bump + embedded-broker harness + shared Schedule conformance helper) → meta-fanout-lifecycle → webhook-forwarder (Shape A) → engine switch (default off) → the rest, lowest risk first; cmd/worker last.

**Decisions of record:**
1. **Class rule — long-running handlers cannot use server-owned ladders:** server normalization forces `ackWait = backoff[0]`, and `KeepInProgress` caps heartbeat extension at ~5×AckWait, so a fast first rung starves handlers whose work time ≫ rung (cmd/worker: 30m syncs vs a 2m30s cap). Such consumers keep **single-owner client scheduling**, validated by `jsconsumer.Schedule` (empty violations). Mixed ownership remains forbidden — that was the ENT-1535 defect; pure client ownership is not.
2. **Exit criterion amended:** "0 hand-rolled fetch loops **except cmd/fanout's two pooled consumers**" — jsconsumer's serial Consume + prefetch-discarding Stop cannot host the 8-worker pools without duplicate git syncs (1s dedup window on mirror_git_v1). {"id":"COR-1270","title":"webhook-forwarder and fanout run a 41h orphaned BackOff ladder no code declares (live ENT-1535, prod)","description":"## What was found

Measured 2026-08-14 during Track D's loop-1 pre-flight, via `natsctl -- consumer info webhooks_github_v1 <durable> --json` on **prod us-east-2** and **staging us-west-2** (identical on both):

| durable | code declares | server actually stores | real envelope |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `webhook-forwarder` | no `BackOff`, client `NakWithDelay(30s)` | `backoff: [30s, 2m, 10m, 1h, 4h, 12h, 24h]` | **41h12m30s** |
| `fanout-us-east-2` / `fanout-us-west-2` | no `BackOff`, client `NakWithDelay(30s)` | same 7 rungs | **41h12m30s** |
| `core-fanout` | no `BackOff` | absent | 3m30s — agrees |
| `meta-fanout` | no `BackOff` | absent | 3m30s — agrees |
| `trails-fanout-push` | no `BackOff` | absent | 3m30s — agrees |
| `trails-fanout-pull-request` | no `BackOff` | absent | 3m30s — agrees |

Two of the seven `webhooks_github_v1` consumers carry a server-side redelivery ladder that **no source file declares**, alongside a client-side `NakWithDelay(30s)`. That is mixed ownership — the <issue id="57d2a8d9-c2a6-49c4-8014-8a67857ef1b0" href="https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/ENT-1535/entire-search-the-ent-1492-dlq-doesnt-prevent-the-stall-a-poison-ref">ENT-1535</issue> defect — live in production.

Because the requested Nak delay equals `BackOff[0]` (both 30s), the server's stretch term is zero on the first rung and redeliveries then follow the **server** ladder exactly. So the real give-up envelope is **41h12m30s**, against `cmd/webhook-forwarder/forwarder.go:48-52`, which states: *"No* `nats.BackOff` *is set, so this is a free choice — not clamped to a schedule."*

## How it got there

`consumerMaxDeliver`'s own comment names the mechanism without drawing the conclusion: *"dropping* `nats.BackOff` *is tolerated (BackOff is not part of that comparison)."* It is tolerated by nats.go's `checkConfig`, which is exactly why the ladder survived its deletion from the source — legacy `PullSubscribe` **binds** to an existing durable and never updates it. So a ladder removed from code stays on the server forever.

The four durables that never carried a ladder never acquired an orphan. This is a history artefact, not a config decision — nobody chose 41 hours.

## Why it matters, independent of Track D

A delivery that keeps failing (entire-web 5xx, network error) holds the `webhooks_github_v1` **ack floor for up to 41 hours**. That stream is interest-retention with seven consumers, and a pinned floor is the <issue id="57d2a8d9-c2a6-49c4-8014-8a67857ef1b0" href="https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/ENT-1535/entire-search-the-ent-1492-dlq-doesnt-prevent-the-stall-a-poison-ref">ENT-1535</issue>/Aug 5–6 shape: the stall signal cannot distinguish one pinned message from a throughput collapse.

It is a **stall, not a loss**: 41h12m30s < the stream's 96h `maxAge`, so the delivery still reaches DLQ capture on delivery 8.

**Second finding — nothing observes this today.** The only per-consumer monitor on this stream (`monitor_ingest_consumer_backlog.tf`) fires on `num_pending + num_ack_pending > 5000` sustained over 20m — a *volume* signal, sized for the 2026-06-01 orphaned-durable starvation. A single message pinning the floor for 41h leaves `num_ack_pending` at 1 and never trips it. Unlike `repo_refs_v1`, `webhooks_github_v1` has **no ack-floor-age monitor at all**, so this behaviour is not merely undocumented — it is unmeasured.

1. **Decide the intended envelope.** Options span 3m30s (a declared flat 30s ladder), ~42m (the entire-search shape `[5m, 5m, 5m, 12m, 15m]`), and ~4h (bounded but patient). The real question is how long an entire-web outage should be absorbed automatically versus dead-lettered for manual replay — `webhooks_github_dlq` retains 7 days in prod, and replay is a manual `mirrorctl` operation.
2. **Make it declared, not inherited.** Whichever envelope is chosen, it has to be written where the code says it is. Reconciling an existing durable's `BackOff` needs `CreateOrUpdateConsumer` (the modern client) — which is precisely what the Track D migration of these two loops does, so the fix and the migration can be the same change if the timing suits.

Next should be a short stop-the-line hardening slice before Loop 2.

1. Fix the production finding in `go-nuts`:

   - `jsconsumer.Run` must recreate a missing durable even when nats.go emits `no responders`/heartbeat failures without closing the consume context.
   - Readiness must represent the local consume loop, not merely a durable recreated by another replica.
   - Add a real-broker regression with two runners and two timed consumer deletions, matching AP South.

2. Release `go-nuts`, bump mirror-pipeline, and roll `meta-fanout` again normally.

3. Then proceed with the planned Loop 2: migrate `webhook-forwarder`. That should also resolve [COR-1270](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-1270/webhook-forwarder-and-fanout-run-a-41h-orphaned-backoff-ladder-no-code):

   - replace its accidental 41-hour ladder with an explicit policy;
   - I recommend roughly 42 minutes—enough to absorb routine outages without pinning the ack floor for nearly two days;
   - add the missing ack-floor-age monitor in the same change.

After that, the approved sequence is the default-off engine switch, remaining low-risk consumers, and `cmd/worker` last.

I’d make the go-nuts recovery fix a blocking child of [COR-1254](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-1254/track-d-consumer-standardization-jsconsumer-everywhere-durables-as) and start there.

content.text: do we need to fix it? or can we leave with it?
do we need to fix it? or can we leave with it?

We can leave the current deployment running; it is healthy, and the mixed old/new deletion race will not happen on ordinary future deploys.

But we should fix the library before migrating another consumer.

Why:

- `jsconsumer.Run` promises recovery when its durable disappears; production proved that promise is incomplete.
- A future operator deletion, stream recreation, or controller event could trigger the same stuck state.
- Another replica can recreate the shared durable and make a deaf pod appear Ready.
- Standardizing more consumers now would replicate that weakness across the fleet.

So my recommendation is:

- No emergency rollback or hotfix.
- Keep the current rollout.
- Treat the `go-nuts` recovery change as a blocker for Loop 2.
- Until fixed, the operational recovery is sequential pod recycling.

It’s safe to leave briefly; it’s not a good defect to knowingly multiply.

The trails returned an issue: ```### Medium finding

**Location:** `cmd/meta-fanout/lifecycle.go:373`

Setting `BackOff` here means `jsconsumer.Config.validate`/`Start` now runs `checkAgainstStream`, which fetches `STREAM.INFO` for `resource_lifecycle_v1` on every (re)start attempt — a JetStream API call the pre-migration `PullSubscribe`-based consumer never made. # Escalation Requests

Commands are run outside the sandbox if they are approved by the user, or match an existing rule that allows it to run unrestricted. The command string is split into independent command segments at shell control operators, including but not limited to:

- Pipes: |
- Logical operators: &&, ||
- Command separators: ;
- Subshell boundaries: (...), $(...)

Each resulting segment is evaluated independently for sandbox restrictions and approval requirements.

Example:

git pull | tee output.txt

This is treated as two command segments:

["git", "pull"]

["tee", "output.txt"]

Commands that use more advanced shell features like redirection (>, >>, <), substitutions ($(...), ...), environment variables (FOO=bar), or wildcard patterns (*, ?) will not be evaluated against rules, to limit the scope of what an approved rule allows.

## How to request escalation

IMPORTANT: To request approval to execute a command that will require escalated privileges:

- Provide the `sandbox_permissions` parameter with the value `"require_escalated"`
- Include a short question asking the user if they want to allow the action in `justification` parameter. e.g. "Do you want to download and install dependencies for this project?"
- Optionally suggest a `prefix_rule` - this will be shown to the user with an option to persist the rule approval for future sessions.

If you run a command that is important to solving the user's query, but it fails because of sandboxing or with a likely sandbox-related network error (for example DNS/host resolution, registry/index access, or dependency download failure), rerun the command with "require_escalated". ## When to request escalation

While commands are running inside the sandbox, here are some scenarios that will require escalation outside the sandbox:

- You need to run a command that writes to a directory that requires it (e.g. running tests that write to /var)
- You need to run a GUI app (e.g., open/xdg-open/osascript) to open browsers or files.

When choosing a `prefix_rule`, request one that will allow you to fulfill similar requests from the user in the future without re-requesting escalation. It should be categorical and reasonably scoped to similar capabilities. You should rarely pass the entire command into `prefix_rule`.

            # trails-fanout — US-only secondary-event producer. It consumes
            # pull_request and push subjects from the raw webhooks_github_v1
            # stream on two dedicated durables, resolves repo placements

            # events into every placement's local NATS island. The identity is
            # authorized in base because the US workload cross-publishes into
            # peer EU/AP cells. It also captures exhausted/malformed deliveries

            # ENTIRE_WEBHOOK_DLQ_ENABLED. It has no max-delivery advisory
            # listener, so no advisory subscribe grant is present.
            - user: "trails-fanout"
              permissions:
                publish:
                  allow:
                    - "trail_forge.v1.>"
                    - "webhooks.github.dlq.trails-fanout"
                    - "$JS.API.>"

                    # trails-fanout-push and trails-fanout-pull-request) — see

                    - "webhooks.>"

            # jetstream-controller — the nack JetStream controller

            # reconciles Stream CRDs against this server, so streams are
            # declared in git rather than created imperatively by
            # mirror-pipeline binaries. Touches only the JetStream API, never
            # app subjects. $JS.API.> can be tightened to $JS.API.STREAM.>
            # (+ $JS.API.CONSUMER.> if Consumer CRDs are ever adopted). Cert
            # DNS SAN "jetstream-controller" (internal-tls component) is what
            # verify_and_map keys on. Added ahead of the controller so the
            # user is in place before anything authenticates as it; harmless
            # until then (an unused user grants nothing).
            - user: "jetstream-controller"
              permissions:
                publish:
                  allow:
                    - "$JS.API.>"
                subscribe:
                  allow:

                allow_responses: true

                    - "repo_refs_v1.>"

                    # S3 code-search index. Least-privilege: only the
                    # repo.deleted subtype, not the whole stream.
                    - "resource_lifecycle_v1.repo.deleted"

            - user: "tlog-viewer"
              permissions:
                subscribe:
                  allow:
                    - "repo_refs_v1.>"
                    - "_INBOX.>"
                allow_responses: true
            # entire-ci-webhooks — outbound consumes repo_refs_v1.> (RFD-018 MVP);
                    - "webhooks.github.dlq.>"
                    - "$JS.API.>"
                    # Explicit ack grant for this user's webhooks_github_v1 pull
                    # consumer. allow_responses below covers only ONE reply within
                    # ~2m of delivery, so an ack issued outside that window is
                    # rejected — "Publish Violation ... $JS.ACK.webhooks_github_v1.>"
                    # — and a rejected ack leaves the message unsettled, so it
                    # redelivers and the work repeats; on a poison message it pins

                    # pushes acks past the window: this was observed on
                    # webhook-forwarder, core-fanout and fanout during the 2.14.4
                    # roll of eks-prod-us-east-2 (2026-08-10, COR-1223), and
                    # meta-fanout / trails-fanout carry the same latent gap.

                    - "$JS.ACK.webhooks_github_v1.>"

                    - "$JS.EVENT.ADVISORY.CONSUMER.MSG_TERMINATED.webhooks_github_v1.>"
                allow_responses: true
            # fanout — pull-subscribes webhooks.> (US cells) and repo_refs_v1.>

                    - "webhooks.github.dlq.>"

                    - "$JS.ACK.repo_refs_v1.>"
                    # Ack for its webhooks_github_v1 consumer (durable

                    # allow_responses is not enough.

                    # backstop re-captures a delivery the inline DLQ path dropped

                    # per-region durable name. The GetMsg refetch publishes to
                    # $JS.API.STREAM.MSG.GET.webhooks_github_v1, already covered by
                    # $JS.API.> above (the stream isn't AllowDirect).
                    - "$JS.EVENT.ADVISORY.CONSUMER.MAX_DELIVERIES.webhooks_github_v1.>"
                    - "$JS.EVENT.ADVISORY.CONSUMER.MSG_TERMINATED.webhooks_github_v1.>"
                allow_responses: true
            # meta-fanout — consumes webhooks_github_v1 (star/fork/repository
            # events) on its own durable (a 2nd consumer alongside fanout) and
            # publishes per-placement github_meta.v1.<jur>.<cluster>
            # display-metadata plus github_pr.v1.<jur>.<cluster> pull-request
            # activity. Runs in US but cross-publishes github_meta.v1.> /
            # github_pr.v1.> into peer cells' NATS (EU/AP), so every cell's NATS
            # must authorize this identity to publish — hence base, not a US-only
            # overlay. Cert DNS SAN "meta-fanout" (internal-tls component,
            # SPIFFE_NAME "meta-fanout") is what verify_and_map keys on. Does NOT
            # publish mirror.> — that's fanout's git-sync output, not
            # meta-fanout's.
            # Also enqueues onto the dedicated github_meta_backfill work-queue:
            # the backfill one-shot JS-publishes jobs to github_meta_backfill.>
            # and the same identity's separate durable drains them via $JS.API.>.
            #

// checkAgainstStream re-runs the schedule check with the stream's retention
// filled in, which [Config.validate] cannot know: a ladder that outlives
// max_age never reaches its own dead-letter branch, because the stream
// discards the message first. That is silent data loss dressed as a retry
// policy, and it is only visible with both halves in hand.
//
// A stream this cannot read is an error, not a pass. That distinction is the
// whole value of the check: it exists to stop a consumer whose ladder outlives
// retention from starting, so answering "fine" whenever the retention is
// unknown removes the protection in exactly the case where nothing else
// supplies it. Reading the stream and creating the consumer are separate
// JetStream API subjects ($JS.API.STREAM.INFO.> and $JS.API.CONSUMER.>), so a
// credential can be able to do the second and not the first — and then a
// swallowed error means the invalid ladder starts and the source expires the
// message before capture, which is the ENT-1492 loss this check promises to
// prevent.
//
// The legitimate case still rides out, but through the classifier rather than
// through a blanket pass: a stream that does not exist yet — the
// declarative-provisioning race — surfaces as [jetstream.ErrStreamNotFound],
// which [isRetryableStartError] already treats as retryable, so [Run] keeps
// waiting for the stream to appear exactly as before. A denied
// STREAM.INFO publish gets no reply and times out, which is retryable too: the
// consumer never starts, [Run] logs the failure on every attempt, and the safe
// outcome is a consumer that is loudly absent rather than quietly unchecked.
func (c Config) checkAgainstStream(ctx context.Context, js jetstream.JetStream) error {
	if c.Retry == nil && len(c.BackOff) == 0 {
		return nil
	}
	// js.Stream fetches STREAM.INFO to build the handle, so the config is
	// already in hand — a second Info call would be one more round trip and one
	// more failure mode on the startup path.
	stream, err := js.Stream(ctx, c.Stream)
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer(%s): read stream %q to check the ladder against its retention: %w", c.Name, c.Stream, err)
	}
	info := stream.CachedInfo()
	if info == nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer(%s): stream %q returned no config to check the ladder against its retention", c.Name, c.Stream)
	}
	sched := c.schedule()
	sched.StreamMaxAge = info.Config.MaxAge
	if err := sched.Err(); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer(%s): %w", c.Name, err)
	}

// checkAgainstStream re-runs the schedule check with the stream's retention
// filled in, which [Config.validate] cannot know: a ladder that outlives
// max_age never reaches its own dead-letter branch, because the stream
// discards the message first. That is silent data loss dressed as a retry
// policy, and it is only visible with both halves in hand.
//
// A stream this cannot read is an error, not a pass. That distinction is the
// whole value of the check: it exists to stop a consumer whose ladder outlives
// retention from starting, so answering "fine" whenever the retention is
// unknown removes the protection in exactly the case where nothing else
// supplies it. Reading the stream and creating the consumer are separate
// JetStream API subjects ($JS.API.STREAM.INFO.> and $JS.API.CONSUMER.>), so a
// credential can be able to do the second and not the first — and then a
// swallowed error means the invalid ladder starts and the source expires the
// message before capture, which is the ENT-1492 loss this check promises to
// prevent.
//
// The legitimate case still rides out, but through the classifier rather than
// through a blanket pass: a stream that does not exist yet — the
// declarative-provisioning race — surfaces as [jetstream.ErrStreamNotFound],
// which [isRetryableStartError] already treats as retryable, so [Run] keeps
// waiting for the stream to appear exactly as before. A denied
// STREAM.INFO publish gets no reply and times out, which is retryable too: the
// consumer never starts, [Run] logs the failure on every attempt, and the safe
// outcome is a consumer that is loudly absent rather than quietly unchecked.
func (c Config) checkAgainstStream(ctx context.Context, js jetstream.JetStream) error {
	if c.Retry == nil && len(c.BackOff) == 0 {
		return nil
	}
	// js.Stream fetches STREAM.INFO to build the handle, so the config is
	// already in hand — a second Info call would be one more round trip and one
	// more failure mode on the startup path.
	stream, err := js.Stream(ctx, c.Stream)
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer(%s): read stream %q to check the ladder against its retention: %w", c.Name, c.Stream, err)
	}
	info := stream.CachedInfo()
	if info == nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer(%s): stream %q returned no config to check the ladder against its retention", c.Name, c.Stream)
	}
	sched := c.schedule()
	sched.StreamMaxAge = info.Config.MaxAge
	if err := sched.Err(); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer(%s): %w", c.Name, err)
	}

item.stdout:
entire session attach — Attach an existing agent session
Attach an existing agent session that wasn't captured by hooks.

This creates a checkpoint from the session's transcript and links it to the
last commit. Use this when hooks failed to fire or weren't installed when
the session started, or to attach a research session.

If the last commit already has a checkpoint, the session is added to it.
Otherwise a new checkpoint is created.

Use --review to tag the attached session as an agent review. The
first user prompt in the transcript is recorded as the review prompt.
Pass --skills to declare which skills were actually run; omit to
attach a review without a declared skills list.

Works with any registered agent, including external agents enabled via
external_agents in settings. Run 'entire agent list' to see the full list.

If --agent doesn't locate a transcript, Entire auto-detects the agent from
the transcript and prints the detected agent name.

Current repo: gh/entireio/go-nuts  (auto-detected from origin; pass --repo only for a DIFFERENT repo)

Flags:
  -a, --agent string     Agent that created the session (see 'entire agent list' for registered agents, including external) (default "claude-code")
  -f, --force            Skip confirmation and amend the last commit with the checkpoint trailer (best-effort; if the amend fails the checkpoint is still created and the trailer is printed for manual paste)
      --review           Tag the attached session as an agent review
      --skills strings   Optional: declare which review skills were run in this session. Only used with --review
